xs: A **satellite-based navigation constellation** is not listed among IGMDP spin-offs — option **(1)**.
The listed spin-offs are the **long-range tracking system**, **composites**, **ring laser gyros** and **radomes**.
xa: **Agni-IV** uses a **ring-laser-gyro INS** with **RINS + MINGS** navigation.
IGMDP was **launched in 1983** and **completed in 2008**.
Nodal lab: **DRDL Hyderabad**.

10.s: Why is the Integrated Guided Missile Development Programme regarded as significant?
o: Ended all missile development in India after the completion of Prithvi.
Turned India from a missile importer into a missile-exporting power and formed a base for later Agni-V MIRV, BMD and BrahMos-era programmes.
Restricted India to importing surface-to-air missiles from foreign suppliers.
Was created exclusively for developing civilian launch vehicles.
10.x: The IGMDP transformed India from a missile importer into a missile-exporting power and provided the foundation for Agni-V MIRV, ballistic missile defence and BrahMos-era programmes.
10.tq: Select the option that captures both the strategic transformation and the later technological base.
xs: IGMDP turned India from a **missile importer** into a **missile-exporting power**, and laid the base for **Agni-V MIRV, BMD and BrahMos-era programmes** — option **(2)**.
Missile work did not end: after **2008**, later missiles came as **separate projects**.
xa: Launched in **1983** under **Dr APJ Abdul Kalam**, after the **1962, 1965, 1971** wars.
**Mission Divyastra (2024)**: Agni-V with **MIRV**.
Spin-offs: **long-range tracking system**, **composites**, **ring laser gyros**, **radomes**.

10.s: In which year was the Integrated Guided Missile Development Programme (IGMDP) officially completed?
10.x: IGMDP ran from 1983 and was officially completed in 2008; later missiles became separate projects.

10.s: In which year was the Integrated Guided Missile Development Programme launched?
10.x: IGMDP was launched in 1983 under Dr APJ Abdul Kalam and was officially completed in 2008.

10.s: Which missiles were developed in the first phase (1984-89) of the IGMDP?
10.x: Prithvi and Trishul came in the first phase (1984-89); Nag and Akash in 1989-92; Agni matured by 2008.

10.s: Which among the following cricketers has been inducted to ICC Hall of Fame?
10.src: APPSC Assistant Telugu Translator General Studies & Mental A
10.x: Sachin Tendulkar was inducted into the ICC Cricket Hall of Fame in 2019.

10.s: What is the name of the navy sailor from India, who participated in Golden Globe Race and was rescued by a French fishing vessel when his boat was damaged in deep waters recently?
10.src: APPSC Teaching Staff of the Department of Technical Educatio
10.x: Commander Abhilash Tomy of the Indian Navy was injured when his yacht was damaged during the 2018 Golden Globe Race and was rescued with help from the French fisheries patrol vessel Osiris.

10.s: What is the name of the Medium Range Surface to Air Missile jointly developed by India and Israel?
10.src: APPSC Assistant Director of Fisheries in A.P. Fisheries Serv
10.x: Barak-8 (MRSAM) is the medium-range surface-to-air missile developed jointly by DRDO and Israel Aerospace Industries. BrahMos is India-Russia, Pinaka a rocket launcher.

10.s: Out of the following, Dhanush is
o: A mini nuclear reactor using Thorium fuel
A long range ballistic missile to be used by Army
A short range ballistic missile to be used by Navy
A satellite to study the interstellar matter
10.src: APPSC Royalty Inspector, Agriculture Officer, Town Planning
10.x: Dhanush is the naval, ship-launched version of Prithvi – a short-range ballistic missile for the Navy, not an Army long-range missile, a reactor or a satellite.

10.s: What is the strike range of Agni-IV ballistic missile in kilometres?
10.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Screening Test 2017
10.x: Agni-IV is an IRBM of about 3,500-4,000 km range, so 3,000-4,000 km is the matching option; 4,000-5,000 km overshoots it.

10.s: The width of the Himalayas varies from 400 km in Kashmir to ............ in Arunachal Pradesh.
10.x: NCERT gives the width as 400 km in Kashmir narrowing to 150 km in Arunachal Pradesh (NextGen's figures are 500 km to 200 km). With 400 km in the stem, the answer is 150 km.

10.s:
Consider the following communication technologies:

A. Closed-circuit Television

B. Radio Frequency Identification

C. Wireless Local Area Network
Which of the above are considered Short-Range devices/technologies?
10.x: CCTV, RFID and wireless LAN all operate as short-range devices under the short-range-device (SRD) category, so all three (UPSC 2022 key d).

10.s: The name of the Strategic Ballistic Missile launched by the Defence Research and Development Laboratories in the recent past is
10.x: Agni-III (about 3,500 km) is a strategic ballistic missile, tested successfully in 2007, 2008 and 2010. Nag (anti-tank) and Trishul (SAM) are tactical, and Prithvi-II is a short-range tactical missile.

10.s: 'Eye in the sky' is the name given to:
o: AWACS-Airborne Early Warning and Control System
10.x: AWACS (Airborne Warning and Control System) aircraft are called the "eye in the sky" because their rotating radar watches a wide airspace. Sukhoi and MiG are fighters and Agni-III is a missile.

10.s:
Regarding Agni-III which is/are correct?

a. It is a surface-to-surface ballistic missile

b. Its range is 3,500 kms

c. While the first flight of Agni-III in 2006 failed, its second and third flights in 2007 and 2008 were successful.
10.x: Agni-III is a surface-to-surface ballistic missile of about 3,500 km range; its first flight (9 July 2006) failed and the second (April 2007) and third (May 2008) succeeded. So all three statements are correct.

10.s:
Consider the following statements :

A. In November, 2006, DRDO successfully conducted the interception test using Prithvi II missile.

B. Prithvi-II is a surface-to-surface missile and can be deployed to guard the metros against air attacks.
Which of the statements given above is / are correct?
10.x: On 27 November 2006 DRDO's PAD interceptor (a modified Prithvi) destroyed a Prithvi-II target – the interception test of statement A. Prithvi-II is an offensive surface-to-surface missile, not a weapon to guard metros against air attack, so B is wrong.

10.s: One of the purpose of INSAT 1D, the satellite put up by Indian Scientist, is to link all parts of India by television. The height about the earth surface at which it is revolving is about
10.x: INSAT-1D, like every INSAT, is geostationary, about 36,000 km above the equator.

10.s: Which one of the following is the correct description of AGNI Missile, which is developed by Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO)?
10.x: Agni is a family of long-range surface-to-surface ballistic missiles (about 700 km to over 5,000 km). It is not short-range and not described as "the fastest missile".

10.s:
Which of the following are related to Agni-V missile?

A. Intercontinental ballistic missile (ICBM)

B. Solid fuelled ballistic missile

C. Four stage missile

D. Air to surface launchable missile
Choose the correct answer:
10.x: Agni-V is a solid-fuelled surface-to-surface ballistic missile of 5,000 km+ (often called ICBM), so A and B; it has three stages (not four) and is not air-launched.

10.s:
The major success of the Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) has been in the missile programme. So far it has successfully test-fired the following missiles for the defence forces.

A. Prithvi: Surface to surface missile

B. Trishul: Surface to Air missile

C. Akash: Surface to Air missile

D. Nag: Anti-tank guided missile

E. Agni: Sea launched cruise missile
Select the correct answer from the codes given below:
o: A, B, C and D only
10.x: Prithvi is surface-to-surface, Trishul and Akash are surface-to-air and Nag is an anti-tank guided missile, so A-D are correct. Agni is a land-based surface-to-surface ballistic missile, not a sea-launched cruise missile, so E is wrong.

10.s: Find the incorrect pair
10.x: Nag is a third-generation fire-and-forget anti-tank missile, not a surface-to-air missile, so that pair is incorrect. Prithvi and Agni are surface-to-surface and Trishul is surface-to-air.

10.s: Which one of the following is a Submarine-Launched Ballistic Missile (SLBM)?
10.x: K-4 is a submarine-launched ballistic missile (~3,500 km) of the K-series for the Arihant-class submarines. Agni-4 and Prithvi are land-based and Akash is a SAM.

10.s: India’s short-range missile is –
10.x:
Official key / most books: Nag (shortest range). Strictly: Prithvi is the missile formally classed as a short-range ballistic missile (SRBM) (PMF S&T Part 6 (src/science-tech/pmf-science-tech-06.txt) p.62).
Among the options Nag has the shortest range (500 m – 4 km), so most keys give Nag. Prithvi (150-350 km) is formally India's short-range ballistic missile, Agni is long-range and Arjun is a tank.

10.s: India’s surface to air missile is –
10.x: Trishul is a short-range, low-level surface-to-air missile of the IGMDP. Agni and Prithvi are surface-to-surface and Nag is anti-tank.

10.s: Which of the following is India's surface to surface defence missile –
10.x: Prithvi is India's surface-to-surface short-range ballistic missile. Trishul and Akash are surface-to-air and Nag is anti-tank.

10.s: What is the range of Prithvi, a liquid-fuelled surface-to-surface short-range ballistic missile?
10.x: Prithvi is a surface-to-surface SRBM with a range of 150–350 km and uses liquid fuel.
xa: ⚠ **Prithvi = liquid**; **Agni = solid**.
**Prithvi-I** (Army) **150 km**; **Prithvi-II** (Air Force) **350 km**.
**Dhanush** = naval, **ship-launched** version of Prithvi.
The name Prithvi means **Earth**.

10.s: At about what speed does Akash, a medium-range surface-to-air missile, travel?
10.x: Akash is a medium-range SAM with a range of about 25-30 km, a speed of about Mach 2.5 and an altitude capability of 18 km.
xa: Base Akash: launch weight **720 kg**.
**Akash Prime**: indigenous **active RF seeker**; **Akash-NG**: about **70 km**, canister-launched.
⚠ **Akashteer** (BEL + Army) is an air-defence **control** system, NOT a missile.

10.s: Which missile has a range of about 25–30 km?
10.x: Akash, a medium-range SAM, has a range of about 25–30 km. Trishul reaches about 9 km, Nag 500 m to 4 km (land version), and Agni about 700 km to over 5,000 km.

10.s: What is Agni-VI in the context of India's missile programme?
10.x: Agni-VI is described as a proposed longer-range intercontinental ballistic missile.
10.tq: Distinguish a proposed future system from operational Agni variants.
xs: **Agni-VI** is a **proposed longer-range ICBM** — option **(1)**.
The **naval version of Prithvi** is **Dhanush**; the interceptor is **PAD / Pradyumna**.
xa: **Agni-V**: **5,000+ km**, below the **5,500 km** ICBM threshold, so formally **IRBM** class.
Agni is developed by **DRDO** — ⚠ not ISRO (APPSC **2019**).
**Agni-P (Prime)**: **1,000-2,000 km**, new-generation **canisterised**.

10.s: Which one of the following statements about Trishul is NOT correct?
o: Its commonly cited range is about 9 km.
It was inducted into regular service after successful development.
It is a short-range, low-level surface-to-air missile.
It uses solid fuel with thrust vector control.
10.x: Trishul was never inducted into regular service and the programme was closed in 2008. It is a short-range low-level SAM using solid fuel with thrust vector control.
10.tq: Find the wrong service-status statement rather than the missile’s technical features.
xs: Statement (2) is NOT correct: **Trishul** was **never inducted** and was **closed in 2008** — option **(2)**.
The other statements are correct: range about **9 km**, a **short-range, low-level SAM**, **solid fuel with thrust vector control**.
xa: Trishul was shut on **27 Feb 2008** after failing operational requirements, with **delays** and **cost overruns**.
Replacements: **Spyder** (IAF), **Barak-1** (Navy), **Akash** (Army).
Indigenous successor: **QRSAM** (Quick Reaction SAM).
Trishul means **Trident**.

10.s: Which was the first missile developed under the IGMDP?
10.x: Prithvi was the first IGMDP missile; Prithvi-I serves the Army and Prithvi-II the Air Force.
xa: **Prithvi-III / Dhanush** serves the **Navy** (ship-launched).
Prithvi-II was **first tested in 1996** and **inducted in 2003**.
Prithvi-II and Agni-I were **test-fired together** (**Jul 2025**).

10.s: Which type of fuel do Prithvi-I and Prithvi-II use?
10.x: Prithvi-I and Prithvi-II use liquid fuel, whereas Agni-I uses solid fuel.
xa: Prithvi-II and Agni-I were test-fired together in **Jul 2025**.
**Agni-I**: single-stage solid, about **700-800 km**, about **15 m** long.
An **Agni-1** test was held at **ITR Balasore** on **22 May 2026**.

10.s: HELINA is the helicopter-launched version of which missile?
10.x: HELINA is the helicopter-launched Nag, a fire-and-forget anti-tank missile.
xa: Nag: **IIR** seeker and an **8 kg HEAT tandem warhead**.
**NAMIS** (Nag Mk-2) is also fire-and-forget — the tracked "**tank killer**".
⚠ "Which is a fire-and-forget anti-tank missile?" → **Nag** (not Prithvi, Akash or Trishul).

10.s: Which of the following missile names is NOT correctly matched with its meaning?
10.x: Trishul means Trident; it is Agni that means Fire.

10.s: Which services use the Akash surface-to-air missile?
10.x: Akash, a medium-range SAM of about 25-30 km, is used by the Army and the Indian Air Force.

10.s: Rashtriya Avishkar Abhiyan launched on 9th July 2015 by
10.src: APPSC Endowment Subordinate Service (Mains) Paper-I General
10.x: The Rashtriya Avishkar Abhiyan, the MHRD programme to make school children curious about science and maths, was launched by Dr APJ Abdul Kalam on 9 July 2015 at Vigyan Bhawan.

10.s: Which of the following islands has been renamed as Abdul Kalam Island?
10.src: APPSC Divisional Accounts Officer (Mains) General Studies &
10.x: Wheeler Island off Odisha, India's missile test site, was renamed Dr APJ Abdul Kalam Island in 2015.

10.s: An assumption or proposition whose validity is to be tested is known as
10.src: APPSC Assistant Telugu Translator General Studies & Mental A
10.x: A hypothesis is a tentative assumption or proposition whose validity is to be tested by research.

10.s: In the PURA model (Provision of Urban Amenities in Rural Areas) model proposed by President APJ Abdul Kalam did not propose the following connectivity?
10.src: APPSC ASO Mains General Studies & Mental Ability 2017
10.x: Kalam's PURA rests on physical, electronic and knowledge connectivity leading to economic connectivity; cultural connectivity is not one of them.

10.s: In which place, recently Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated the Abdul Kalam Memorial?
10.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-I General St
10.x: PM Modi inaugurated the Dr APJ Abdul Kalam National Memorial at Pei Karumbu, Rameswaram (Kalam's birthplace), on 27 July 2017.

10.s: The missile 'Agni-II' has a range of
10.x: Agni-II has a range of about 2,000-2,500 km (NextGen: 2,500 km), so 2,000 km is the right option; 700-1,000 km is Agni-I and 200 km Prithvi.

10.s: India successfully test-fired the "Agni" missile on 9th January, 2003. Which of the following is not true about it?
o: It was fired from Wheeler Island
It is a two-stage missile variant
10.x: The 9 January 2003 test from Wheeler Island was of Agni-I, the short-range single-stage variant (about 700 km). So "it is a two-stage missile variant" is the untrue statement; Agni-II is the two-stage one.

10.s: On December 11 India tested indigenously designed SANT missile at
10.x: DRDO and the IAF flight-tested the helicopter-launched SANT (stand-off anti-tank) missile from the Pokhran ranges, Rajasthan, on 11 December 2021. Balasore/Chandipur and Thiruvananthapuram were not the site.

10.s: Which among the following ballistic missiles was tested successfully by India in December 2016?
10.x: Agni-V was test-fired on 26 December 2016 from Dr APJ Abdul Kalam (Wheeler) Island, its fourth test and first canister test from a full mobile launcher. Agni-IV was tested on 2 January 2017.

10.s: The range of AGNI-IV is
10.x: Agni-IV has a range of about 3,500-4,000 km, so 3,000-4,000 km is the matching option.

10.s: Which of the following Missiles will be test fired by ISRO in next year with range capacity of 5000 km?
10.x: Agni-V has a range of 5,000+ km, matching the question; it is built by DRDO, not ISRO (the stem is wrong there). Agni-VI is still under development, and Agni-III and Agni-IV have shorter ranges (about 3,500 km and 4,000 km).

10.s: Mission 'Divyastra' is related to which of the following?
10.x: Mission Divyastra (11 March 2024) was the first flight test of Agni-V with MIRV technology – several warheads on one missile, each aimed at a different target. It is not about Prithvi, a mounted gun or a reconnaissance vehicle.

10.s: An indigenously manufactured missile with a range of 700 km was successfully tested by India in March, 2010. How is it known ?
10.x: The 700 km nuclear-capable missile tested from Wheeler Island on 28 March 2010 was Agni-I. Prithvi-I and II are 150 km and 350 km; Agni-II is 2,000 km+.

10.s: Which one of the following facts about Agni-5 missile is not correct ?
o: It can be fired from any place
It has a firing range of up to 5000 km
It cannot be captured by Radar of enemies
10.x: Agni-V (5,000+ km) is a fully indigenous DRDO missile, so "not exclusively indigenous" is the incorrect statement. Being canister-based and road-mobile, it can be fired from almost anywhere.

10.s: The approx. range of Agni-II missile is –
10.x: Agni-II is a two-stage solid missile with a range of 2,000-2,500 km (NextGen: 2,500 km), so about 2,000 km is the best option.

10.s: The name 'Agni' is related with –
o: A machine to fight with fire
10.x: Agni is a surface-to-surface ballistic missile developed by India under the IGMDP, conceived by Dr APJ Abdul Kalam; it is not a fire-fighting machine, a tank or an aircraft.

10.s: The ICBM developed by India, with a strike range of more than 2000 km, is given the name :
10.x:
Official key / most books: Agni-II (the "ICBM" of the stem). Strictly: Agni-II is an MRBM; Agni-V is India's ICBM (PMF S&T Part 6 (src/science-tech/pmf-science-tech-06.txt) p.64).
Of the options only Agni-II has a range above 2,000 km (2,000-2,500 km). Strictly it is a medium-range missile, not an ICBM; Prithvi is short-range and Trishul and Akash are SAMs.

10.s: Which force operates India's Agni missiles, built by DRDO?
10.x: Agni is DRDO-built, fully indigenous and operated by the Strategic Forces Command.
xa: In **Aug 2026**, conventional missiles (incl. **Nag**) went to private industry via ToT; **Agni** stays in **state production**.
Agni means **Fire**.
**Mission Divyastra (2024)**: Agni-V with **MIRV**.

10.s: Which of the following describes Agni-I?
o: Two-stage liquid-fuel missile of about 2,000–3,000 km range
Single-stage solid-fuel missile of about 700–800 km range
Single-stage liquid-fuel missile of about 150 km range
Three-stage solid-fuel missile of about 5,000 km range
10.x: Agni-I is a single-stage solid-fuel missile with a range of about 700–800 km and is approximately 15 metres long.
10.tq: Identify the missile from its stage, fuel and range combination.
xs: **Agni-I** is a **single-stage solid-fuel** missile of about **700-800 km** range — option **(2)**.
It is about **15 m** long, with accurate navigation.
**2,000-3,000 km** is **Agni-II** (two-stage solid); **150 km** liquid is **Prithvi-I**; **5,000 km** three-stage is **Agni-V**.
xa: Agni-I is **nuclear-capable**, fired by the Army from **road-mobile TEL** trucks.
Agni-I test: **ITR Balasore**, **22 May 2026**.
⚠ Some notes give Agni-I as **~700-900 km** (SRBM/MRBM).

10.s: How many stages does Agni-V, a solid-fuel, canister-launched missile, have?
10.x: Agni-V is a three-stage solid-fuel, canister-launched missile with a stated range of 5,000 km or more; MIRV has been tested with it.
xa: Agni-V is **fully indigenous** — ⚠ "not exclusively indigenous" is the wrong statement (UPPSC **2015**).
**Dr Tessy Thomas** played a key role in Agni-V.
⚠ Formally **IRBM** class: the ICBM threshold is **5,500 km**.

10.s: Which of the following pairs about the Agni series is correctly matched?
10.x: Agni-II is a two-stage solid-fuel missile (2,000–3,500 km). Agni-IV is two-stage and road-mobile (about 4,000 km), Agni-III has about 3,500 km range, and the three-stage canisterised missile is Agni-V.

10.s: From which platform was Agni-Prime test-fired on 24 September 2025?
10.x: Agni-Prime, a canisterised 1,000–2,000 km missile, was fired from a rail-based mobile launcher.
xa: Agni series operator: **Strategic Forces Command**.
**Agni-4** user trial: **ITR Chandipur, 6 Aug 2026**.
An advanced Agni with **MIRV** was tested on **8 May 2026**.

10.s: Mission Divyastra (2024) tested MIRV technology on which missile?
10.x: Mission Divyastra, conducted in 2024, flight-tested Agni-V with Multiple Independently targetable Re-entry Vehicles (MIRVs).
xa: Advanced Agni with a **MIRV** was tested on **8 May 2026**.
Agni-V: **three-stage solid**, **canister-launched**, **5,000+ km**.
All 2026 Agni tests were under the **Strategic Forces Command**.

10.s: What is the formal ICBM range threshold that places Agni-V's 5,000 km range in the IRBM class?
10.x: The ICBM threshold cited is 5,500 km, so Agni-V is formally an IRBM, though some sources call it an ICBM.
xa: **Agni-VI** is the **proposed longer-range ICBM**.
Agni-V is **three-stage solid** and **canister-launched**.
Advanced Agni with a **MIRV** was tested on **8 May 2026**.

10.s: Which Agni variant is a two-stage, road-mobile missile with a range of about 4,000 km?
10.x: Agni-IV is two-stage and road-mobile with about 4,000 km range; Agni-V is three-stage with 5,000+ km.

10.s:
Consider the following statements with respect to 'NCC Flag':

a. NCC Flag Contains NCC Crest in gold in the middle, with the letters "NCC" encircled by a wreath of seventeen lotus with a background in Red, Blue and Light blue.

b. Red depicts the Navy, Deep Blue depicts the Army and Light Blue depicts the Air Force.

c. The seventeen lotuses represent the 17 State Directorates. "Unity of Discipline" (Ekta aur Anushasan) is written at the bottom of the NCC Flag.
Which of the above statements are correct?
10.src: APPSC Forest Section Officer General Studies & Mental Abilit
10.x: Statement b is wrong: in the NCC flag red stands for the Army, deep blue for the Navy and light blue for the Air Force. The crest with 17 lotuses (17 State Directorates) and the motto 'Unity and Discipline' (Ekta aur Anushasan) are as stated.

10.s: From which of the following place the indigenously developed Quick Reaction Surface-to-Air Missile (QRSAM) was test fired successfully in July 2017?
10.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-I General St
10.x: QRSAM, the indigenous quick-reaction SAM, was test-fired from the Integrated Test Range at Chandipur, Odisha, in 2017. Sriharikota is ISRO's launch port and Kalpakkam a nuclear site.

10.s:
Match the following

A. Supreme Commander - i. Arup Raha

B. Army General - ii. Sunil Lamba

C. Navy Admiral - iii. Pranab Mukherjee

D. Air Chief Marshal - iv. Dalbir Singh Suhaag
10.x:
all four posts have changed — now President Droupadi Murmu; Army Chief Gen. Dhiraj Seth, Navy Chief Adm. Krishna Swaminathan (Praveen CA-360 Aug/Jun 2026), IAF Chief Air Chief Marshal Ashutosh Dixit from 31 Oct 2026 (daily CA 31 Oct 2026)
In 2016 the Supreme Commander was President Pranab Mukherjee, Army Chief Gen. Dalbir Singh Suhag, Navy Chief Adm. Sunil Lanba and Air Chief Marshal Arup Raha (now President Droupadi Murmu; Army Gen. Dhiraj Seth, Navy Adm. Krishna Swaminathan, IAF Air Chief Marshal Ashutosh Dixit).

10.s: If Russia equipped the Indian Air Force with the Sukhoi-30 K, who equipped the Sukhoi-30 K with the avionics and weapon systems?
10.x: Israel supplied much of the avionics, navigation and weapon fit of India's Sukhoi-30 jets (with France and India); the USA, Sweden and Norway did not.

10.s:
In respect of the 'Exercise Garuda VII' (2022) which of the following are correct?

A. It was held at the Air Force Station, Prayagraj

B. It was a bilateral exercise

C. Indian Air Force (IAF) and French Air & Space Force (FASF) participated in the exercise

D. The aim is to enhance operational capability of both the countries

E. The exercise provides a platform for sharing best practices
o: A, B, C and D only
B, C, D and E only
10.x: Garuda VII (26 Oct – 12 Nov 2022) was a bilateral exercise of the IAF and the French Air and Space Force to enhance operational capability and share best practices. It was held at Air Force Station Jodhpur, not Prayagraj, so A is wrong.

10.s:
Read the following statements :

a. Abhinandan Varthaman is the Indian Air Force (IAF) Air Commander

b. He is the first recipient of the 'Bhagwan Mahavir Ahimsa Puraskar'.

c. The award carries a cash prize of Rs.5 lakh.
Which of the Statements is/are not correct?
10.x: Abhinandan Varthaman was a Wing Commander (not Air Commander), so a is wrong; he was the first recipient of the Bhagwan Mahavir Ahimsa Puraskar (2019), but the award carried Rs 2.51 lakh, not Rs 5 lakh, so c is wrong too.

10.s: Choose the correct match (Army - Navy - Airforce)
o: Major-General - Rear Admiral - Air Vice Marshal
10.x: Major-General (Army) = Rear Admiral (Navy) = Air Vice Marshal (IAF). The others are mismatched: Captain = Lieutenant = Flight Lieutenant, Major = Lieutenant Commander = Squadron Leader, Colonel = Captain = Group Captain.

10.s: Name the missile tested by Indian scientists and defence personnel on 27.1.96 at Chandipur :
10.x: Prithvi-II was first test-fired on 27 January 1996 from Chandipur. Prithvi-I was tested in 1988, Akash is a SAM and PSLV-D2 a launch vehicle.

10.s: In which year was Prithvi-II, first tested in 1996, inducted?
10.x: Prithvi-II was inducted in 2003; the naval version is Dhanush.
xa: Prithvi-II: **350 km**, payload **500-1,000 kg**, **nuclear-capable SRBM**.
Dhanush means **Bow**.
**PAD / Pradyumna** is the Prithvi-based exo-atmospheric interceptor.

10.s: Which service operates Dhanush, the ship-launched version of the Prithvi missile?
10.x: Dhanush (Prithvi-III) is the Navy's ship-launched Prithvi; Prithvi-I is the Army's 150 km version.

10.s: Which service operates Prithvi-II, the variant with a range of about 350 km?

Trishul's range: ~**9 km** (some notes **12 km**).

10.s: On which date was Akash Prime, an upgraded Akash Mk-I with an indigenous active RF seeker, first tested?
10.x: Akash Prime was first tested on 27 September 2021.

10.s: What is the approximate range of the canister-launched Akash-NG?

Base Akash: **Mach 2.5**, **18 km** altitude.

10.s: In the context of Trishul's replacement, which pair of service and missile system is correctly matched?

**Akash** serves both the **Army and Air Force**.

10.x: QRSAM, or Quick Reaction Surface-to-Air Missile, is the later indigenous short-range successor to Trishul.

xs: The indigenous successor to Trishul is **QRSAM** (Quick Reaction SAM) — option **(4)**.
**Barak-1** was the **Navy**'s replacement (imported); **Prithvi** is a ballistic missile.
⚠ **BrahMos** (India-Russia) was **not part of IGMDP**.
xa: Other replacements: **Spyder** (IAF), **Akash** (Army).
Trishul: quick-reaction SAM, **above Mach 2**, never inducted.

10.s: Which radar does Akash Mk-I use for command guidance?
10.x: Akash Mk-I relies on command guidance and the Rajendra radar.

3. It was inducted into the Army.

10.x: Trishul is a short-range quick-reaction SAM of about 9 km range, but it was never inducted and was shut in 2008.

10.s: What is Akashteer, developed by BEL with the Indian Army?
10.x: Akashteer is an air-defence control system, not a missile.

10.s: What is meant by the term 'fire-and-forget' in missile technology?
o: The missile is incapable of changing its course after launch.
The missile can guide itself after launch, allowing the operator to take cover.
The missile is fired only after the target has been destroyed by another weapon.
The missile must remain continuously controlled by the operator until impact.
10.x: A fire-and-forget missile guides itself after launch, enabling the operator to seek cover or perform another task.
10.tq: Translate the technical term into its operational consequence.
xs: **Fire-and-forget**: the missile **guides itself after launch**, so the operator can **take cover** — option **(2)**.
Examples: **Nag**, **HELINA**, **MPATGM**.
xa: **Top attack**: missile climbs, then dives onto the tank's thin **top armour**.
**Nag** has both **top-attack** and **direct-attack** modes.
Nag is a **third-generation** fire-and-forget ATGM (APPSC **2018** key).

10.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
10.x: Nag uses an Imaging Infra-Red seeker, whereas Akash Prime uses an active RF seeker and SANT uses Lock-On After Launch. Therefore, Nag with an active RF seeker is not correctly matched.
10.tq: Find the one swapped seeker associated with a different missile.
xs: **Nag — active RF seeker** is wrongly matched — option **(4)**.
Nag uses an **Imaging Infra-Red (IIR)** seeker; the **active RF seeker** belongs to **Akash Prime**.
**SANT** uses **Lock-On After Launch** — correctly matched.
xa: **Akash Prime** = upgraded **Akash Mk-I**, first tested **27 Sep 2021**.
**Akash Mk-I** uses command guidance with the **Rajendra radar**.
Other guidance types: **laser**, **GPS**, **electro-optical**.

10.s: What is Nag Mk-2, the tracked fire-and-forget 'tank killer' approved for Army procurement, called?

xa: **NAMICA** = tracked amphibious **Nag Missile Carrier**, carries up to **six** missiles.
**HELINA** (about **7 km**) is for **Army Aviation**.
**SANT** range: **15-20 km**.

10.s: For which service is HELINA, the helicopter-launched variant of the Nag missile, meant?
10.x: HELINA is the helicopter-launched Nag variant for Army Aviation, whereas Dhruvastra is intended for the Indian Air Force.
xa: ⚠ Remember: **HELINA** = Army Aviation; **Dhruvastra** = IAF.
HELINA is a **fire-and-forget** missile, like Nag and MPATGM.
**SANT** is the **air-launched stand-off** ATGM (**15-20 km**).

10.s: Each Nag Missile Carrier (NAMICA) can carry up to how many missiles?
10.x: Each NAMICA, a tracked amphibious vehicle, can carry up to six Nag missiles.
xa: Nag is a **third-generation fire-and-forget ATGM** (APPSC **2018** key), range **4-7 km**.
Its **Imaging Infra-Red (IIR)** seeker gives **night-strike** capability.
**Nag Mk-2 / NAMIS** — tracked "**tank killer**", approved for Army procurement (**2026**).
⚠ NAMICA is a **carrier vehicle**, not a missile.

10.s: What does an anti-tank missile generally do in the top-attack mode?
o: Approaches at ground level and hits the side armour
Climbs and then dives onto the tank's thinner top armour
Strikes the thick frontal armour head-on
Hits the tracks to immobilise the tank
10.x: In top attack, the missile climbs and then dives onto the tank's thinner top armour; Nag has both top-attack and direct-attack modes.
xa: Nag's **IIR** seeker gives **night-strike** capability.
**SANT** uses a **Lock-On After Launch** seeker.
Not missiles: **Arjun** (tank), **Pinaka** (rocket launcher), **NAMICA** (Nag carrier).

10.s: For which service is Dhruvastra, the helicopter-launched Nag variant, meant?
10.x: HELINA is the Army Aviation version, while Dhruvastra is the IAF version.

10.s: Which guidance mode does SANT, the air-launched stand-off anti-tank missile, use?
10.x: SANT (15–20 km) uses Lock-On After Launch (LOAL).

10.s: What is the range of the Nag-family MPATGM, a man-portable anti-tank missile?
10.x: MPATGM reaches about 2.5 km; NAMIS reaches 7–10 km and SANT 15–20 km.

10.s: The Nag anti-tank missile uses which type of seeker?
10.x: Nag uses an IIR seeker; Akash Prime uses an active RF seeker.

Consider the following pairs:

10.s: Who is considered the 'Missile Woman' of India?

10.x: Dr APJ Abdul Kalam led the Integrated Guided Missile Development Programme (1983), India's indigenous missile programme. Raja Ramanna and M.G.K. Menon were nuclear and science administrators; "U.S. Rao" is a distractor.

10.s: By what name is Dr Tessy Thomas, who played a key role in Agni-V, popularly called?
10.x: Dr Tessy Thomas, the 'Missile Woman of India', played a key role in Agni-V and is called 'Agniputri'.
xa: **Agni-V**: **three-stage solid**, **canister-launched**, range **5,000+ km**, **MIRV** tested.

10.x: Kalam was CSA at Pokhran-II in 1998, not Pokhran-I.

10.x: Agni-V was test-fired from Wheeler Island (renamed Dr APJ Abdul Kalam Island in 2015) off Odisha. "Missile", "Rocket" and "Defence" Island are not real names.

SLV-III, under his direction, launched Rohini

xa: **Agni-4** user trial: **ITR Chandipur**, **6 Aug 2026**.
**Agni-1** test: **ITR Balasore**, **22 May 2026**.
Kalam is the "**Missile Man of India**", who led IGMDP from **1983**.

o: Dr APJ Abdul Kalam Island — Rajasthan
Integrated Test Range, Chandipur — Andhra Pradesh

Kurnool range hosted the **ULPGM-V3** trials (**2026**).
Kalam was Chief Scientific Adviser at **Pokhran 1998**.

10.src: Grama Ward Sachivalayam Category-III Village Fisheries Assis

11.s: What is the speed of air flow in a Scramjet before combustion?
11.src: APPSC Dental Asst. Surgeons, Zilla Sainik Welfare Officers,
11.x: In a scramjet (supersonic combustion ramjet) the air stays supersonic through the combustor; in a ramjet it is slowed to subsonic.

11.s: BrahMos is a ____
11.src: APPSC Forest Section Officer General Studies & Mental Abilit
11.x: BrahMos is a supersonic cruise missile (Mach 2.8-3.0), jointly developed by DRDO and Russia's NPO Mashinostroyeniya.

11.s:
Consider the following statements:

a. Ballistic missiles are jet-propelled at subsonic speeds throughout their flights, while cruise missiles are rocket-powered only in the initial phase of flight.

b. Agni-V is a medium-range supersonic cruise missile, while BrahMos is a solid-fuelled intercontinental ballistic missile.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
11.x: Both are wrong: ballistic missiles are rocket-powered and follow a ballistic arc after boost, while cruise missiles are jet-powered through most of the flight; Agni-V is a ballistic missile (IRBM/near-ICBM) and BrahMos a supersonic cruise missile.

11.s: The clock speed of a processor is measured in which of the following units?
11.x: Processor clock speed is measured in hertz, today in gigahertz; Mach and knots are speeds and megabytes storage.

11.s: Which of the following statements is incorrect regarding the BrahMos Missile?
o: It has a range of 1200 km
It has been jointly made by India and Russia
It is operational with Indian Army, Navy and Airforce
11.src: Grama Ward Sachivalayam Category-III Animal Husbandry Asst.
11.x: BrahMos range was 290 km originally and about 450-800 km in extended-range versions, never 1,200 km. It is supersonic, Indo-Russian and in service with all three services.

11.s: Which of the following is a supersonic cruise missile?
11.x: BrahMos is the supersonic cruise missile; Agni-I, Agni-III and Prithvi-II are ballistic missiles.

11.s: Which one of the following statements best reflects the idea behind the "Fractional Orbital Bombardment System" often talked about in media?
o: A hypersonic missile is launched into space to counter the asteroid approaching the Earth and explode it in space.
A spacecraft lands on another planet after making several orbital motions.
A missile is put into a stable orbit around the Earth and deorbits over a target on the Earth.
A spacecraft moves along a comet with the same speed and places a probe on its surface.
11.x: FOBS puts a nuclear warhead into a partial (fractional) low Earth orbit and de-orbits it onto a target, so it can come from an unexpected direction such as over the South Pole (UPSC key c).

11.s: Which one of the following statements best reflects the idea behind the 'Fractional Orbital Bombardment System' often talked about in media?
o: A hypersonic missile is launched into space to counter
A spacecraft lands on another planet after making
A missile is put into a stable orbit around the Earth
A spacecraft moves along a comet with the same speed
11.x: Same UPSC 2022 item: FOBS = a missile/warhead put into (fractional) orbit that de-orbits over a target on Earth.

11.s: Which type of missile stays powered throughout its flight and uses aerodynamic lift at relatively low altitude?
11.x: A cruise missile is powered throughout; a ballistic missile is powered mainly in boost phase and then follows a high parabolic arc.
xa: Ballistic examples: **Agni**, **Prithvi**, **Pralay**.
Cruise examples: **BrahMos**, **Nirbhay**.
⚠ **Pralay** is **quasi-ballistic** with **manoeuvrable re-entry**.

11.s: Which of the following characterises a scramjet engine?
o: Subsonic combustion after the air is slowed down
Supersonic combustion and no rotating parts
Carrying all the oxygen needed for combustion
11.x: A scramjet uses supersonic combustion and has no rotating compressor or turbine parts; unlike a rocket, it does not carry its oxidiser.
xa: HSTDV flew at **Mach 6+**, with thermal protection above **2,000°C**.
**Jan 2026**: a scramjet combustor ran **over 12 minutes**.
Compare **SFDR** (solid fuel ducted ramjet): also uses **atmospheric air** for combustion.

11.s: For which of the following is Solid Fuel Ducted Ramjet (SFDR) technology mainly intended?
11.x: SFDR uses atmospheric air for combustion and was demonstrated from ITR Chandipur for application in long-range air-to-air missiles.
11.tq: Match the propulsion system with its stated operational application.
xs: **SFDR** (solid fuel ducted ramjet) is meant for **long-range air-to-air missiles** — option **(2)**.
It uses **atmospheric air for combustion** and was demonstrated from **ITR Chandipur**.
xa: **Astra Mk-3 'Gandiva'** is being built with an **SFDR** engine, range **350+ km**.
⚠ **BrahMos** uses a **liquid ramjet**; SFDR is a **solid fuel** ramjet.
**Astra Mk-2** uses a **dual-pulse solid motor** (about **200 km**).

11.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about MIRV and Mission Divyastra?
o: Mission Divyastra used the K-4 missile
Mission Divyastra used the Agni-V missile
A MIRV lets one missile carry several warheads aimed at different targets
Mission Divyastra was India's first MIRV flight test
11.x: Mission Divyastra used Agni-V, not K-4; K-4 is a submarine-launched missile.

11.s: Which engine powers Nirbhay, India's subsonic long-range land-attack cruise missile?

Code :
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation
Both A and R are true but R is not a correct explanation
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

Printed key: (b) both true, R not the explanation. Many solvers argue (a), since conservation of momentum (R) explains the recoil, and some call A practically false (general knowledge, not checked).

Write off all dues owed to generators

21.s: The maximum efficiency of a distribution transformer is
21.src: APPSC AEE Electrical Engineering Screening Test General Stud

27.s:
Identify the correct pair (s) from the given pairs with respect to types of energy and their definition and choose the correct option.
I. Radiant energy -----energy moving through substances in longitudinal (compression or rarefaction) waves.
II. Chemical energy----- energy stored in the bonds of atoms and molecules
III. Sound energy ---- electromagnetic energy that travels in transverse waves.
o: Only I and III are correct
I, II and III are correct
27.x: Only II is right: chemical energy is stored in the bonds of atoms and molecules. I and III swap the definitions: sound travels in longitudinal waves, radiant energy in electromagnetic transverse waves.

27.s: What type of energy transformation occurs in a hydroelectric power plant?

27.s: A photoelectric cell is a device which :
o: converts light energy into electric energy
converts electric energy into light energy
27.x: A photoelectric (solar) cell converts light energy into electrical energy.

27.s: A device which converts electrical energy into mechanical energy is –
27.x: An electric motor converts electrical energy into mechanical energy; a dynamo does the reverse and a transformer only changes voltage.

27.s: Lightning can even burn a tree because it contains tremendous amount of
27.x: Lightning is a huge electrical discharge; its tremendous electrical energy heats and can burn a tree.

27.s: A dynamo which is said to generate electricity actually acts as a :
27.x: A dynamo does not create charge; it converts mechanical energy into electrical energy, so it is a converter of energy.

27.s: The energy of wind is –
27.x: Wind is moving air, so its energy is only kinetic energy.

27.s: The photoelectric effect was discovered by :
27.x: Heinrich Hertz discovered the photoelectric effect in 1887; Einstein later explained it.

27.s: In wind power, which form of energy is converted into electrical energy?
27.x: Wind turbines convert the kinetic energy of wind into mechanical and then electrical energy.

27.s: Which of the following energy changes involves frictional force?

27.x: Work against friction turns kinetic energy of motion into heat; potential-to-sound and chemical-to-heat changes do not need friction.

27.s: The energy, found in dry cell is –

18.x: Uranium (U-235) is the fuel of nuclear reactors. Thorium is only fertile and must first be bred into U-233; radium is not a reactor fuel and 'nuclear water' does not exist.

18.s: Which one of the following is used as moderator in a nuclear reactor ?
18.x:
Printed key / most books: (b) Heavy water. Strictly, (d) ordinary water is also a moderator, in light-water reactors (PMF S&T Part 4 p.38).
Heavy water slows neutrons without absorbing many, so it is the classic moderator. Ordinary (light) water is a moderator too, in PWRs and BWRs, which is why the book lists '(b) & (d)'. Thorium and radium are not moderators.

18.s: The mass number of a nucleus is :
o: the sum of the numbers of neutrons and protons
the total mass of neutrons and protons
always more than the atomic weight
always less than its atomic number
18.x: Mass number is the number of protons plus neutrons (the nucleon count). It is a count, not the total mass, and it is not always more or less than other quantities.

18.s: The atoms, in which the number of protons is same but the number of neutrons is different, are known as –
18.x: Atoms with the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons are isotopes. Isobars share the mass number, isotones the neutron number.

Number of protons is same but number of neutrons is
Number of both protons and neutrons is same
Number of both protons and neutrons is different
18.x: Isotopes have the same number of protons (atomic number) but different numbers of neutrons. Same neutrons, different protons describes isotones.

Atomic number and atoms mass both are same
18.x: Isotopes of an element have the same atomic number but a different atomic mass (mass number), because their neutron counts differ.

18.x: Graphite slows fast neutrons, so it serves as a moderator; it is not the fuel. Its lubricant use is outside reactors.

18.s: What is the function of moderator in a nuclear reactor?
18.src: APPSC Forest Subordinate Service (Thanedar) Paper-II General
18.x: A moderator slows down neutrons so that they can cause further fission. Absorbing heat is the coolant's job; control rods regulate the rate.

18.s: What happens if the control rods are not used in a nuclear reactor?
o: Chain process would go out of bounds
The reactor will be slow to act
The reactor will continue to work as it is
18.x: Control rods absorb surplus neutrons; without them the chain reaction would go out of bounds rather than stop or slow down.

18.s: The substance used as moderator and coolant both, in nuclear reactors is :
18.x:
Printed key / most books: (a) Ordinary water. Strictly, (b) heavy water is also both moderator and coolant, in PHWRs (PMF S&T Part 4 p.43-44).
Ordinary (light) water is both the moderator and the coolant in PWRs and BWRs. Heavy water does both jobs in PHWRs, which is why the book prints '(a) & (b)'. Liquid ammonia and liquid hydrogen are neither.

18.s: Heavy water is a type of –
18.x: Heavy water is chiefly a moderator that slows neutrons; in PHWRs it also acts as coolant. It is not an ore or a fuel.

18.s: The function of heavy water in a nuclear reactor is to?
o: Slow down the speed of neutrons.
18.x: Heavy water acts mainly as a moderator: it slows fast neutrons to thermal speed while absorbing very few. It does not speed neutrons up or stop the reaction. (In PHWRs it also cools, but 'cool down the reactor' is not the key.)

18.s: The function of heavy water in a nuclear reactor is to
o: Slow down the speed of neutrons
18.x: Heavy water is used as a moderator to slow down the neutrons produced in fission so that the chain reaction can be sustained. It does not increase their speed or stop the reaction.

18.s: In Light Water Reactors, which account for over 85% of world nuclear capacity, what role does light water play?
18.x: LWRs use light water for both moderation and cooling and make up more than 85% of global nuclear capacity.

**Tarapur = BWR**; **Kudankulam = VVER**.

20.x: Radioactive (radiometric) dating measures the absolute age of rocks, not their composition, colour or weight.

20.x: The age of the Earth is measured by the uranium(-lead) process (Patterson); carbon dating covers only ~50,000 years.

20.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about radiometric dating?

20.s: What is the principle behind thermocouple?

20.s: On which effect is the conversion of decay heat into electricity by thermocouples in a radioisotope thermoelectric generator (RTG) based?
20.x: An RTG is not a fission reactor; its thermocouples turn decay heat directly into electricity by the Seebeck effect, so it has no moving parts.

20.s: Which isotope is generally used as fuel in radioisotope thermoelectric generators?

RTGs are **not reactors** — no fission.

A. Baking soda is used to chemically leaven doughs and batters when it is mixed with an acid.

B. Cream of Tarter is one of the powdery acids used in baking powder to help leaven products.

C. Baking powder makes cakes rise by releasing carbon dioxide gas.
25.src: APPSC Executive Officer Gr-III Endowment Paper-I General Stu
25.x: All three are true: baking soda leavens when it meets an acid, cream of tartar (potassium bitartrate) is the dry acid in baking powder, and baking powder releases CO2 that makes the cake rise.

25.s: An example of a phosphoenol pyruvate carboxyl kinase (PEP-CK) type of C4 photosynthesis
25.src: APPSC Forest Section Officer Screening Test General Studies
25.x: Panicum (e.g. Panicum maximum) is the classic PEP-CK type C4 plant; sugarcane and maize are NADP-ME type, Amaranthus NAD-ME type.

25.s:
Consider the following statements:

I. Transpiration is the loss of water from the plant through evaporation at the root surface.

II. Transpiration is the main driver of water movement in the root nodules.

III. Transpiration is caused by the evaporation of water at the leaf-atmosphere interface; it creates negative pressure (tension) at the leaf surface.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are CORRECT?
25.src: APPSC Junior Lecturers, Polytechnic Lecturers Paper-I Genera
25.x: Only III is correct: transpiration is evaporation at the leaf-air interface creating tension that pulls water up; it is not loss at the root surface, and it does not drive water in root nodules.

25.src: APPSC Assistant BC Welfare Officer and Royalty Inspector in

25.src: APPSC Assistant Social, B.C. & Tribal Welfare Officers (Main

25.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Screening Test 2017

25.s: The main component of Gobar Gas is –
25.x: Gobar gas is biogas from cattle dung; its main component is methane (about 50–75%).

25.s: Which of the following is the procedure for a biogas plant–
25.x: A biogas plant works by fermentation (anaerobic digestion) of dung and other wastes.

25.s: A group of archaebacteria is used in the production of:
25.x: Methanogens, a group of archaebacteria, produce methane under anaerobic conditions.

25.s: Cooking gas is mainly –
25.x: Gobar/biogas used as cooking gas is mainly methane. (LPG cooking gas is butane–propane, which is not offered.)

25.s: Biogas mainly consists of –
25.x: Biogas is mainly methane (50–75%) and carbon dioxide (25–50%), with traces of H2S and moisture.

25.s: In biomass gasification, biomass is heated with limited oxygen. What does the resulting syngas mainly consist of?
o: Carbon monoxide, hydrogen and carbon dioxide
Sulphur dioxide, nitrogen dioxide and ammonia
25.x: Controlled or limited-oxygen gasification produces syngas containing carbon monoxide, hydrogen and carbon dioxide.
25.tq: Use the gas-composition clue and distinguish syngas from atmospheric air.
xs: Biomass gasification gives **syngas** of **carbon monoxide, hydrogen and carbon dioxide** (CO + H2 + CO2) — option **(2)**.
Biomass is heated with **controlled (limited) oxygen**.
xa: Syngas runs **engines/power**.
⚠ **Pyrolysis** is heating in the **absence** of oxygen.
Gasification is **decentralised**, uses farm residue and cuts **stubble burning**.

25.s: Producer gas is a mixture of carbon monoxide, hydrogen, carbon dioxide and which other gas?
25.x: Producer gas is a mix of CO, H₂, CO₂ and methane.
n: Producer gas or synthetic gas is a mixture of carbon monoxide, hydrogen, carbon dioxide and methane. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #36 · pp 62-64]
Bio-asphalt is a renewable construction material. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #36 · pp 62-64]
Bio-asphalt is a non-petroleum construction material. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #36 · pp 62-64]
xa: **Biomass gasification** heats biomass with **limited oxygen** → **syngas**.
**Pyrolysis** yields **biochar**, **bio-oil** and **syngas**.
Source **segregation** is essential for gasification and anaerobic digestion.

25.s: What is Compressed Biogas (CBG)?
o: Unpurified biogas stored at atmospheric pressure
Compressed carbon dioxide used as a fuel
Purified and compressed biogas chemically identical to CNG
25.x: CBG is purified and compressed biogas. Chemically, it is identical to compressed natural gas and is considered renewable and carbon-neutral.
25.tq: Separate CBG from raw biogas and from similarly named fossil-fuel gases.
xs: **CBG** is **purified, compressed biogas**, **chemically identical to CNG** — option **(3)**.
It is renewable and carbon-neutral, promoted under **SATAT**.
xa: **SATAT** was launched in **2018** by **MoPNG**.
CBG progress remains "limited" despite SATAT, even as **90%** of LPG imports pass **Hormuz**.
Draft **CAFE III** norms (from **Apr 2027**) let makers claim credit for **ethanol, CBG**.

25.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about a Microbial Fuel Cell?
o: It cleans wastewater and generates electricity simultaneously
Microorganisms in it act as catalysts
It converts the chemical energy of organic substrates into electricity
It burns organic matter to raise steam for a turbine
25.x: A microbial fuel cell does not burn anything: its microbes convert the chemical energy of organic matter directly into electricity while cleaning wastewater.
n: Microorganisms act as catalysts in a microbial fuel cell. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #26 · pp 45-47]
A microbial fuel cell converts the chemical energy of organic substrates into electricity. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #26 · pp 45-47]
A microbial fuel cell can help clean wastewater and generate electricity simultaneously. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #26 · pp 45-47]
A microbial fuel cell can be used in wastewater treatment. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #26 · pp 45-47]

25.s:
Consider the following statements:
I. Food-processing residues are biomass sources relevant to waste.
II. Human sewage is a biomass source relevant to waste.
III. Biogenic municipal solid waste is a biomass source relevant to waste. Which of the statements given above are correct?
25.x: All three are biomass sources from waste: food-processing residues, human sewage and the biological part of municipal waste.
25.tq: Recall the biomass sources from waste.
n: Food-processing residues are biomass sources relevant to waste. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #26 · pp 45-47]
Human sewage is a biomass source relevant to waste. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #26 · pp 45-47]
Biogenic municipal solid waste is a biomass source relevant to waste. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #26 · pp 45-47]
xs: **All three — I, II and III** — are correct — option **(4)**.
**Food-processing residues**, **human sewage** and **biogenic municipal solid waste** are **biomass sources** relevant to waste.
**Biogenic MSW** serves as **biomass feedstock**.
xa: **Agricultural waste** and **animal manure** are also biomass sources.
**Biomethanation**: microbes convert wet organic waste → **biogas**.
**RDF** = **refuse-derived fuel**, the dry combustible part of segregated MSW.

25.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about biogas?
o: Methane makes up about 85–95% of biogas
It is mainly methane and CO2 from anaerobic digestion of organic matter
Its methane is formed by methanogenic archaea in the absence of oxygen
The slurry left after digestion is a good organic manure
25.x: Methane is about 50–75% of biogas; 85–95% is the methane share of piped natural gas.
xa: **Gobar gas** is biogas from **cattle dung** — biomass energy (APPSC 2019).
**Jashbhai Patel**'s floating-drum "**Gramalakshmi**" plant was popularised by **KVIC**.
**CBG** is purified biogas, **chemically identical to CNG**.

25.s: Which organisation popularised the 'Gramalakshmi' floating-drum gobar gas plant of Jashbhai Patel?
25.x: The 1950s Gramalakshmi plant was popularised by KVIC, not MNRE.
xa: **Gobar gas** = biogas from cattle dung; it is **biomass energy**.
MNRE runs the **Biogas Programme** under the **National Bioenergy Programme 2021-26** for small/medium rural plants.
**GOBARdhan** (**2018**) is the umbrella for cattle dung → biogas/bio-CNG.

25.s: Which of the following describes biomass energy?
o: Solar energy stored by plants through photosynthesis
Energy obtained from tidal currents alone
Heat stored only in the Earth's mantle
25.x: Biomass energy represents solar energy captured and stored by plants through photosynthesis. It may be burned directly or converted into biogas and biofuels.
25.tq: Trace the energy source through the biological conversion chain.
xs: **Biomass energy** is **solar energy stored by plants** through **photosynthesis** — option **(1)**.
It is burned directly or converted to **biogas/biofuels**.
Earth's internal heat is **geothermal**; tidal currents are **ocean energy** — not biomass.
xa: **Gobar gas** is biomass energy (**APPSC 2019**).
Agricultural waste: **crop residue** (stubble, paddy-husk), **manure**, **cattle dung**, **dairy waste** — all biodegradable.
**Biomass gasification**: biomass heated with **controlled oxygen** → **syngas** (CO + H2 + CO2).

25.s: Which of the following is an example of biomass energy?
25.x: Gobar gas is biomass energy because it is produced from organic material, especially cattle dung.
xa: **Nuclear** is non-fossil but **not renewable**.
Biogas is produced by **anaerobic digestion**; methane ~**50-75%**.
The **"Gramalakshmi"** floating-drum gobar gas plant was by **Jashbhai Patel** (**1950s**).

25.s: Which microbes produce biogas through anaerobic digestion?
25.x: Biogas comes from anaerobic digestion by methanogens in the absence of oxygen.

25.s: What does bagasse cogeneration in sugar mills produce?
25.x: In bagasse cogeneration, sugar mills burn bagasse to produce steam and power together.

25.s: For what is the slurry left after biogas production used?
25.x: The slurry left after biogas production is a good organic manure.

25.s: What is the approximate methane content of biogas?
25.x: Biogas is about 50–75% methane; piped natural gas is 85–95% methane.

25.s: Which of the following is an example of a renewable resource?
25.src: APPSC Assistant Environmental Engineer and Analyst Grade-II
25.x: Biomass is renewable; coal, natural gas and petroleum are fossil, non-renewable fuels.

25.x: Brazil (sugarcane ethanol, mandatory blending since 1976) is regarded as the world's first sustainable biofuel economy.

25.x: Second-generation computers (1956-63) were the first to use transistors in place of vacuum tubes.

25.s: Third generation bioethanol is obtained from ______.
25.x: Third-generation (3G) biofuels come from algae/algal biomass; food crops are 1G, wood residue and energy crops 2G.

25.s:
It is possible to produce algae-based biofuels, but what is/are the likely limitation(s) of developing countries in promoting this industry?
1. Production of algae-based biofuels is possible in seas only and not on continents.
2. Setting up and engineering the algae-based biofuel production requires a high level of expertise/technology until the construction is completed.
3. Economically viable production necessitates the setting up of large-scale facilities which may raise ecological and social concerns.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:

25.s:
It is possible to produce algae-based biofuels, but what is/are the likely limitations of developing countries in promoting this industry?
1. Production of algae-based biofuels is possible in seas only and not on continents.
2. Setting up and engineering the algae-based biofuel production requires a high level of expertise/ technology until the construction is completed.
3. Economically viable production necessitates the setting up of large scale facilities which may raise ecological and social concerns.
Select the correct answer using codes given below:
25.x: Statement 1 is false (algae grow in seas and on land); 2 and 3 are true – high expertise and large-scale facilities that may raise ecological/social concerns.

25.s: Which yeast is used for commercial production of ethanol?
25.x: Baker's yeast Saccharomyces cerevisiae is used for commercial ethanol fermentation; Candida albicans is a pathogen.

25.s: The fourth generation biofuels are obtained from genetically modified :
25.x: Fourth-generation biofuels use genetically modified organisms, chiefly GM algae (also yeast, cyanobacteria).

25.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with the generation of biofuel?
o: 2G — food crops such as sugarcane and corn
25.x: Third-generation biofuels use algae or algal biomass. First-generation fuels use food crops, second-generation fuels use non-food lignocellulosic material, and fourth-generation fuels use genetically engineered organisms.
25.tq: Start with the sure generation–feedstock pair and eliminate the reversed classifications.
xs: **3G** biofuels use **algal biomass** — option **(3)** (PYQ **2023**; APPSC-GS **2023** key).
**1G** uses **food crops** (sugarcane, corn); **2G** uses **non-food lignocellulosic residue** — options (1) and (2) are swapped.
**4G** uses **genetically modified algae/microbes**, not untreated residues.
xa: ⚠ **3G** = algae; **4G** = genetically modified algae/microbes that capture more CO2 (RPSC **2024** key).
3G examples: **algal biodiesel**, **biobutanol**.
**NPB 2018**: 3G biofuels are classed as **advanced biofuels**.

25.s: Which microorganism is associated with the production of bioethanol by fermentation of sugar or starch?
25.x: Saccharomyces cerevisiae, a yeast, ferments sugars or starch-derived sugars to produce bioethanol.
25.tq: Use the organism–product association rather than confusing ethanol with biobutanol production.
xs: Bioethanol is made by fermenting sugar/starch with the yeast **Saccharomyces cerevisiae** — option **(2)**.
**Clostridium acetobutylicum** produces **biobutanol**, not bioethanol.
xa: Biobutanol has a **higher energy density** than ethanol.
⚠ Final methane-forming step in biogas = **methanogenic archaea**.
**1G** bioethanol uses food crops — **sugarcane, molasses, corn, cassava**.

25.s:
Assertion (A): Algae biofuel requires expertise, capital and large-scale facilities.
Reason (R): Algae can be grown on land that is unsuitable for agriculture.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
25.x: Both are true but R does not explain A: growing algae on non-farm land is an advantage, while the need for expertise, capital and large plants comes from the cost and complexity of cultivation and processing.
25.tq: Ask whether R is an advantage or the cause of A.
n: Algae biofuel requires expertise, capital and large-scale facilities. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #36 · pp 62-64]
xs: **Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A** — option **(2)**.
A is true: **algae biofuel** needs **expertise**, **capital** and **large-scale facilities**; it is **not cost-effective**.
R (keyed true) is an advantage of algae; the needs in A come from **high cultivation and harvesting cost** and **energy-intensive lipid extraction**.
xa: Algal advantages: **high yield per unit area**; can use **wastewater and CO2**.
Limitations also include **contamination** and **scale-up** problems.
⚠ **3G** biofuel = **algae**; **4G** = **genetically modified** algae/microbes.

25.s: Which of the following feedstocks is characteristic of second-generation biofuels?
25.x: Second-generation biofuels use non-food lignocellulosic residues such as rice straw, straw, husk, wood chips and bamboo.
25.tq: Classify the feedstock according to whether it is food-based, residual or genetically modified.
xs: **Rice straw** is a **2G** (non-food lignocellulosic) feedstock — option **(4)**.
**Corn grain** and **sugarcane juice** are **1G** food-crop feedstocks; **GM algae** is **4G**.
xa: 2G feedstocks: crop residue, **straw**, **husk**, **wood chips**, **bamboo**, forest waste, non-edible oils.
**IOCL Panipat (2022)** used **rice straw** and **bagasse** — first commercial 2G plant.
2G avoids the **food-fuel conflict** but needs complex thermochemical/biochemical conversion.

25.s: Which of the following is a limitation of algal biofuel?
25.x: Energy-intensive lipid extraction is a limitation; high yield and use of wastewater and CO2 are advantages.
xa: Other limitations: high **cultivation and harvesting cost**, **contamination** and scale-up problems, heavy **water and nutrient** needs.
**CSIR-NIIST** and **DBT-ICT Centre** research algal biofuel.
**3G** biofuels = **algae** (PYQ **2023**).

25.s: Which microorganism is used to produce biobutanol?
25.x: Biobutanol is made with Clostridium acetobutylicum and has higher energy density than ethanol.

25.s: The "Iodine test" is used for testing the presence of?
25.src: Previous paper (title page not in scan)
25.x: Iodine solution turns starch blue-black, so the iodine test detects starch. Sugars, fats and salt give no such colour (fat is tested with paper, sugar with Benedict's reagent).

25.x: RUCO (Repurpose Used Cooking Oil), an FSSAI initiative, collects used cooking oil and converts it into biodiesel.

25.x: Axlewood is Anogeissus latifolia (dhaura), a dry deciduous tree whose tough wood was used for axles. Acacia nilotica is babul, Dalbergia sissoo is shisham and Azadirachta indica is neem.

25.x: Maize is cultivated for ethanol; Jatropha, Pongamia and sunflower for biodiesel.

25.s: Gasohol is a mixture of :

25.s: Biodiesel is commercially produced by which of the following processes?
o: Pyrolysis of lignocellulosic residues without a catalyst
Transesterification of vegetable oils or animal fats with methanol or ethanol
Fermentation of starch by methanogenic bacteria
Electrolysis of water in the presence of vegetable oil
25.x: Biodiesel is produced by transesterifying vegetable oils or animal fats with methanol or ethanol, producing fatty-acid methyl or ethyl esters.
25.tq: Identify the precise conversion process rather than a nearby biofuel process.
xs: Biodiesel is made by **transesterification** of **vegetable oils/animal fats** with **methanol/ethanol** — option **(2)**.
**Pyrolysis** is heating without oxygen (→ biochar, bio-oil, syngas); **fermentation** gives **bioethanol**.
xa: Biodiesel = methyl or ethyl **ester of fatty acids**.
**Palm stearin oil** feeds about **94%** of India's biodiesel (mostly imported).
**Jatropha curcas** seeds give biodiesel (APPSC-GS **2019**).

25.s: Which feedstock accounts for about 94% of India's biodiesel?
25.x: Palm stearin oil accounts for about 94% of India's biodiesel feedstock.
xa: ⚠ **94%** of biodiesel = **palm stearin** (imported), not jatropha.
India has **400+ tree species** bearing **non-edible oilseeds**.
Other feedstocks: rapeseed, soybean, sunflower, animal tallow, **algae**.

25.s: What is India's target for biodiesel blending in diesel by 2030?

25.s: FSSAI's RUCO initiative turns which of the following into biodiesel?

25.x: India's biodiesel blend is still below 0.5%; the target is 5% by 2030.

25.s: What is power alcohol?
o: Fuel-grade ethanol made mainly from molasses
Biodiesel made exclusively from palm stearin oil
Hydrogen produced by electrolysis of water
25.x: Power alcohol refers to fuel-grade ethanol, which in India is made mainly from molasses, a by-product of the sugar industry.

xs: **Power alcohol** is **fuel-grade (anhydrous) ethanol** used as motor fuel, in India made mainly from **molasses** — option **(1)**.
Methane from dung is **gobar gas**; palm stearin feeds **biodiesel**.
xa: **Molasses** is a sugar-industry by-product.

25.s: Where did the Belgian firm VITO launch a two-year biodiesel project in April 2023?
25.x: In April 2023 the Belgian firm VITO launched a two-year biodiesel project at Ayodhya.

25.s: Which is the principal feedstock for ethanol in the United States, the world's largest ethanol producer?
25.x: The US mainly uses maize or corn for ethanol, whereas Brazil mainly uses sugarcane.
xa: India's next blending goal is **E30** by **2030**.

25.s: Under the National Policy on Biofuels 2018, whose approval is needed to use surplus food grains for ethanol production?
o: Ministry of New and Renewable Energy
25.x: Surplus food grains may be converted to ethanol only with NBCC approval (APPSC-G2 2025). FCI supplies the rice but does not approve; MNRE and NITI Aayog are not the approving body under the policy.

xs: **Surplus food grains** may be used for ethanol only with **National Biofuel Coordination Committee (NBCC)** approval — option **(2)** (APPSC-G2 **2025**).

xa: The **2022 amendment** allows **new members** to be added to the NBCC.
**Food vs fuel** debate: sugar prices rising (**Sep 2026**).
Maize-ethanol pricing pulled land from **pulses and oilseeds**.

25.s: Beyond which traditional feedstock did the National Policy on Biofuels, 2018 widen the ethanol feedstock base?

25.s: Which one of the following is NOT an objective of the National Policy on Biofuels?

xs: **Discouraging advanced biofuels** is NOT an objective — option **(4)**; the policy actually boosts **2G/advanced fuels**.

32.x: Yellow street lamps are sodium vapour lamps. Neon glows red, and hydrogen and nitrogen are not lamp fills for street lights.

32.src: APPSC AE (Subordinate Services) Mains General Studies & Ment

33.s: Who coined the term 'floor group'?
33.x: 'Floor group' is a translation of 'status group', a concept of Max Weber.

33.s:
