38.s: In which of the following may grazing of livestock be regulated by the Chief Wildlife Warden?
o: Both National Parks and Wildlife Sanctuaries
38.x: Grazing is fully banned in National Parks; it may be regulated only in Wildlife Sanctuaries.
n: Hunting in a Wildlife Sanctuary is prohibited without permission. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 25-27]
Hunting in a National Park is completely prohibited. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 25-27]
Cattle grazing is completely prohibited in a National Park. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 25-27]
No human activity is permitted in a National Park except activity permitted by the Chief Wildlife Warden. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 25-27]
A protected animal may not be hunted normally. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 25-27]
xa: Both are under the **Wildlife Protection Act, 1972**.
NP boundaries can be altered only on **NBWL** recommendation.
A **Biosphere reserve** allows **settlements** in the transition zone.

38.s: Who declares a Community Reserve?
38.x: The State Government declares a Community Reserve; land already under a national park, sanctuary or conservation reserve cannot become one.
n: Land already designated as a National Park cannot form a Community Reserve. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 25-27]
Land already designated as a Wildlife Sanctuary cannot form a Community Reserve. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 25-27]
Land already designated as a Conservation Reserve cannot form a Community Reserve. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 25-27]
A Community Reserve is declared by the State Government. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 25-27]
xa: Community Reserve = **Section 36C**; added by the **2002** amendment.
⚠ Conservation reserve = **government land**; community reserve = **private/community land**.
First community reserve: **Keshopur-Chhamb (Punjab)**.

38.s: What is the purpose of a Community Reserve?
o: Fauna and flora as well as traditional and cultural values
38.x: A community reserve conserves plants and animals as well as traditional and cultural values.
n: The purpose of a Community Reserve is the conservation of fauna and flora. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 25-27]
A Community Reserve conserves traditional and cultural values. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 25-27]
xa: The State declares it when a **community volunteers**.
It is run by a **CRMC** (Community Reserve Management Committee).
Four PA types: **sanctuary, national park, conservation reserve, community reserve**.

38.s: Which protected-area category is zoned into core, buffer and transition areas?
38.x: A Biosphere Reserve has core, buffer and transition zones; National Parks are clearly demarcated, and sanctuary boundaries are not strictly specified.
xa: The **core** is usually an NP or sanctuary under the **WPA 1972**.
The **buffer** allows research, education, eco-restoration.
The **transition zone** holds settlements, farming, tourism.

38.s: Which one of the following is NOT a feature of an OECM?
o: Recognition automatically changes land ownership and confers new legal authority.
It is demarcated and has inclusive governance.
It is outside the formal protected-area network.
38.x: Recognition of an OECM is outcome-based and does not change land ownership or confer new legal, financial or management authority. The other three are among its criteria.
38.tq: Look for the statement that reverses the no-new-authority feature of an OECM.
xs: OECM recognition does **not** change land ownership or confer legal authority — so option **(1)** is not a feature.
An OECM **confers no legal, financial or management authority**; it is recognised for its **outcomes**.
Options (2), (3) and (4) are among its **4 criteria**: outside PA network, demarcated, inclusive governance, lasting benefits.
xa: OECM = **Other Effective Area-based Conservation Measure**, defined by the **CBD**.
**India's first OECM**: **Aravalli Biodiversity Park, Gurugram (2022)**, a restored mining site.
India's PA share of **5.32%** means **30x30** needs OECMs.

38.s: As of 2026, India's protected-area network comprised how many protected areas?
38.x: The network grew from 981 protected areas in 2020 to 1,134 in 2026, covering 5.32% of India's area.
xa: Break-up: **109 NPs, 573 WLS, 127 Conservation Reserves, 75 Community Reserves**; **58 Tiger Reserves**.
With only **5.32%** under PAs, meeting **30x30** needs **OECMs**.
**Conservation reserves** and **community reserves** were added in **2002**.

38.s: Which of the following pairs is wrongly matched?
o: Conservation Reserve – State-owned land near or linking protected areas
Community Reserve – private or community land voluntarily offered for conservation
National Park – private or community land voluntarily offered for conservation
Tiger Reserve – notified under the NTCA chapter
38.x: Voluntarily offered private or community land forms a Community Reserve; a National Park allows no rights or grazing, and altering its boundary needs NBWL recommendation.
xa: ⚠ Conservation reserve = **government land**; community reserve = **private/community land**.
First community reserve: **Keshopur-Chhamb (Punjab)**.
India has **127 Conservation Reserves** and **75 Community Reserves** (2026).

38.s: The Keshopur-Chhamb community reserve is located in which State?
38.x: Keshopur-Chhamb, India's first community reserve, is in Punjab, not Rajasthan; community reserves came with the 2002 WPA amendment.

38.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about protected areas in India?
o: A Biosphere Reserve is associated with UNESCO's Man and the Biosphere Programme
Biosphere Reserve recognition does not by itself change the legal status or ownership of land
National Parks are established under the Wildlife Protection Act, 1972 through State notification
Wildlife Sanctuaries are established only through UNESCO notification
38.x: Wildlife Sanctuaries are notified by the State under the Wildlife Protection Act, 1972; UNESCO does not notify them.
xa: BR boundaries are zoned **core-buffer-transition**.
NPs are **clearly demarcated**; sanctuary boundaries are **not strictly specified**.
India has **109 NPs** and **573 WLS**.

38.s: On whose recommendation can the boundary of a National Park be altered by a resolution of the State Legislature?
38.x: Under the WPA 1972, a National Park's boundary is altered only by a State Legislature resolution on NBWL recommendation.
38.tq: one-liner

38.s:
Consider the following statements about protected-area categories:
1. A Conservation Reserve is declared on government land.
2. A Community Reserve is declared on private or community land.
3. Amchang is notified as a community reserve.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
38.x: Conservation reserves are on government land and community reserves on private/community land; Amchang is a wildlife sanctuary, not a community reserve.
38.tq: statements

38.s: As of 2026, protected areas cover about what share of India's geographical area?
38.x: India's 1,134 protected areas cover only about 5.32% of its area (Aug 2026).
38.tq: one-liner

38.s: As per the guidelines of Ministry of Environment, Forests and Climate Change, what is the purpose of "Eco Sensitive Zones"?
o: To promote biodiversity in a biome
To promote biodiversity in a habitat
To act as "shock absorbers" for protected areas
To act as training ground for capacity building
38.x: MoEFCC notifies ESZs around national parks and sanctuaries to act as 'shock absorbers' or transition zones. They do not promote biodiversity in a biome and they are not training grounds.

38.s: Which one of the following sets contains only activities classified as REGULATED in an Eco-sensitive Zone?
o: Tree felling, hotels and resorts, road widening
Ongoing agriculture, organic farming, rainwater harvesting
Major hydro projects, commercial mining, ongoing agriculture
38.x: Tree felling, hotels and resorts, and road widening are regulated activities. Commercial mining and major hydro projects are prohibited, while ongoing agriculture, organic farming and rainwater harvesting are permitted.
38.tq: Use category elimination by checking whether each activity belongs to the same regulatory class.
xs: **Tree felling, hotels and resorts, road widening** are **regulated** in an ESZ — option **(1)**.
**Commercial mining, quarrying, polluting industries** and **major hydro projects** are **prohibited**.
**Ongoing agriculture, organic farming, rainwater harvesting** are **permitted**.
xa: ESZ = **"shock absorber"** around an NP or sanctuary.
Notified by **MoEF&CC** under the **EP Act, 1986**.
ESZ width: **up to 10 km** (2011 guidelines).

38.s:
Consider the following statements about Eco-sensitive Zones:
1. They are notified under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986.
2. They are notified under the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
38.x: ESZs are notified under the EP Act, 1986 (Section 3 read with Rule 5 of the EP Rules), not under the WPA, 1972.

38.s: Under the Supreme Court's order, no mining is allowed within what distance of any National Park or Wildlife Sanctuary?
38.x: The Supreme Court barred mining within 1 km of any NP/WLS, unless a larger notified ESZ prevails; 10 km is the MoEF 2011 guideline.
38.tq: one-liner

38.s: Which of the following activities is PROHIBITED in an Eco-sensitive Zone?
38.x: Commercial mining is prohibited in an ESZ; road widening is regulated, and organic farming and rainwater harvesting are permitted.
38.tq: one-liner

38.s:
Which of the following scenarios best illustrates the concept of resource depletion and its long-term impacts on the environment?

A. A forest that is managed sustainably to provide timber while maintaining biodiversity.

B. A coastal area where overfishing has affected the entire marine ecosystem and local communities' livelihoods.

C. A city that implements recycling programmes to reduce waste and promote resource conservation.

D. A national park where strict regulations protect endangered species and their habitats from human interference.
38.src: APPSC Assistant Environmental Engineer and Analyst Grade-II
38.x: Overfishing that harms the whole marine ecosystem and livelihoods is resource depletion with long-term impacts; A, C and D are conservation.

38.s: Protected ecosystems covered 15.2% of land and ____ % of coastal marine areas worldwide by 2014.
38.x: By 2014 protected areas covered 15.2% of land and 8.4% of the marine area under national jurisdiction (coastal-marine). 8.5%, 8.6% and 8.7% are not the reported figure.

38.s: What is an Other Effective Area-based Conservation Measure (OECM)?
o: A temporary area protected only during a breeding season
An ex-situ facility for storing genetic material
An area outside the formal protected-area network that delivers long-term in-situ conservation outcomes
A formally notified National Park with the highest legal protection
38.x: An OECM is outside the formal protected-area network but delivers long-term in-situ conservation outcomes and is recognised on the basis of its results.
38.tq: Use the outside-the-network distinction to separate OECMs from formal protected areas.
xs: An **OECM** is a CBD-defined area **outside the formal PA network** that delivers **long-term in-situ conservation** — option **(3)**.
It is recognised for its **outcomes**, not as a notified National Park.
xa: It **confers no legal, financial or management authority** — land ownership does not change.
**4 criteria**: outside the PA network, demarcated, inclusive governance, lasting benefits.
**India's first OECM**: **Aravalli Biodiversity Park, Gurugram (2022)**.
**APSBB** plans OECMs in sacred groves, greenbelts and wetlands to help meet **30x30**.

38.s: Which organisation maintains the World Database on Protected Areas (WDPA) in collaboration with IUCN?
38.x: The WDPA is run by UNEP-WCMC, based in Cambridge, in collaboration with IUCN, and tracks progress towards the 30x30 target.
38.tq: Use the institutional-identity trap by distinguishing UNEP-WCMC from neighbouring UN bodies.
xs: The **WDPA** is run by **UNEP-WCMC**, Cambridge, with **IUCN** — option **(1)**.
It **tracks 30x30 progress**.
xa: WDPA data (Apr 2026): nearly **10% of the ocean** protected; only **1.66% of the high seas**.
In **2014**, PAs covered **15.2% of land** and **8.4%** of coastal and marine areas.
Marine protection must **triple by 2030**.

38.s: In 2014, what proportion of the world's land area and coastal-marine area was covered by protected areas, respectively?
38.x: In 2014, protected areas covered 15.2% of global land and 8.4% of coastal and marine areas.
38.tq: Use the paired figures carefully and avoid reversing the land and marine percentages.
xs: In **2014**, PAs covered **15.2% of land** and **8.4% of coastal and marine areas** — option **(3)**.
Option (2) reverses the two figures — a common trap.
xa: This was the **APPSC 2018** PYQ benchmark.
Now (WDPA, Apr 2026): nearly **10% of the ocean** protected, only **~3%** fully or highly protected.
**30x30** aims to protect **30% of land and oceans by 2030**.

38.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the present trend in global ocean protection?
o: Nearly 10% of the ocean is protected, but only about 3% is fully or highly protected.
Nearly 30% of the ocean is protected, including 15% that is fully protected.
Only 1.66% of the ocean is protected, while nearly 10% is fully protected.
The proportion of protected ocean area has declined since 2014.
38.x: Nearly 10% of the ocean is protected, but only about 3% is fully or highly protected; merely 1.66% of the high seas is protected.
38.tq: Split the overall figure from the stricter category of fully or highly protected areas.
xs: Nearly **10% of the ocean** is protected, but only **~3%** is **fully or highly protected** — option **(1)**.
**1.66%** is the protected share of the **high seas**, not of the whole ocean, so option (3) is wrong.
Ocean protection has **risen** (up **1.41%** since 2024), so option (4) is wrong.
xa: Marine protection must **triple by 2030** to meet **30x30**.
Data come from the **WDPA**, run by **UNEP-WCMC**, Cambridge, with IUCN.
India has identified **106 ICMBAs** (Important Coastal and Marine Biodiversity Areas).

38.s: What does the '30x30' target of the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework refer to?
o: Generating 30% of electricity from renewable sources by 2030
Protecting 30% of the world's land and oceans by 2030
Reducing greenhouse gas emissions by 30% from 2030 levels
Restoring 30 million hectares of degraded land by 2030
38.x: 30x30 (Target 3 of the KMGBF, CBD COP-15, 2022) aims to protect 30% of land and oceans by 2030. It is not a renewable-energy target (a PYQ trap), nor an emissions-cut or land-restoration target.
38.tq: 30x30 = 30% land + sea protected by 2030 - biodiversity, not energy.
xs: **30x30** means protecting **30% of the world's land and oceans by 2030** — option **(2)**.
⚠ It is **not a renewable-energy target** — a PYQ trap (APPSC G1 2024).
It is **Target 3** of the **Kunming-Montreal GBF** (CBD COP-15, **2022**).
xa: Marine protection must **triple by 2030** to meet it.
**OECMs** help meet 30x30; India's PA share is only **5.32%**.
Nearly **10% of the ocean** is protected today (WDPA, Apr 2026).

38.s: Which of the following best explains the role of Other Effective Area-Based Conservation Measures (OECMs) in relation to the 30x30 conservation objective?
o: They are restricted to marine areas and cannot include community-managed landscapes.
They include only areas inside National Parks and Wildlife Sanctuaries.
They recognise effective conservation areas outside conventional protected areas and can help meet the 30x30 objective.
They replace all Biosphere Reserves recognised under UNESCO's MAB Programme.
38.x: OECMs can cover effectively conserved areas outside reserve forests, National Parks and Wildlife Sanctuaries, including sacred groves, greenbelts and wetlands, and thereby support the 30x30 objective.
38.tq: Apply the distinction between formal protected areas and conservation areas outside them.
xs: **OECMs** recognise effective conservation areas **outside the formal PA network** and help meet **30x30** — option **(3)**.
They lie **outside** NPs and sanctuaries, so option (2) is wrong; they do not replace BRs.
APSBB plans them in **sacred groves, greenbelts, wetlands** — not only marine areas.
xa: India's PA share is only **5.32%** — hence the need for OECMs.
OECMs **confer no legal, financial or management authority**.
**India's first OECM**: **Aravalli Biodiversity Park, Gurugram (2022)**.

38.s: Which of the following is an example of an in-situ method of biodiversity conservation?
38.src: APPSC Dr. NTR University of Health Sciences Mains Paper-II I
38.x: Biosphere reserves conserve species in their natural habitat, so they are in-situ. Zoos, botanical gardens and seed banks are ex-situ.

38.s: How many Biosphere reserves are there in India?
38.src: APPSC Assistant Architectural Surveyor & Deputy Surveyor Gen
38.x: India has 18 notified Biosphere Reserves, 13 of them in UNESCO's World Network (as of 2026).

38.s: Where is the Integrated Coastal and Marine area management Institution located
38.x: The ICMAM (Integrated Coastal and Marine Area Management) Project Directorate of the Ministry of Earth Sciences is in Chennai. Kochi hosts CMLRE, not ICMAM.

38.s: When was the Unique Identification Authority of India (UIDAI) established?
38.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-I General St
38.x: UIDAI was set up on 28 January 2009 as an attached office of the Planning Commission; it became statutory under the Aadhaar Act 2016.

38.s:
Which of the following statements about the Nokrek Biosphere Reserve are true?

A. The Nokrek Biosphere Reserve is located in the northeast of India on the Tura Range, Meghalaya.

B. UNESCO added the Nokrek National park to its list of Biosphere Reserves in May 2009.

C. Nokrek is the highest peak of the Garo Hills rising up 1,412 metres.
38.x: Nokrek BR is on the Tura Range of Meghalaya in Northeast India. UNESCO added it to the World Network in May 2009. Nokrek peak (1,412 m) is the highest in the Garo Hills. All three statements are correct.

38.s: Which of the following is the largest Biosphere Reserve in India?
38.x: The Great Rann of Kutch (Kachchh) BR, 12,454 sq km, is the largest in India, ahead of the Gulf of Mannar (10,500) and the Sundarbans (9,630). Nanda Devi is 5,860 sq km.

38.s: In which of the following places landslides are a frequent hazard?
38.src: Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-I Screening Test 2017
38.x: Uttarakhand's young, steep Himalayan slopes and heavy monsoon rain make landslides a frequent hazard; Tamil Nadu, Madhya Pradesh and Odisha have far lower risk.

38.s: In which year was Chandrayaan I launched?
38.x: Chandrayaan-1, India's first Moon mission, was launched on 22 October 2008 by PSLV-C11.

38.s: LAN stands for
38.x: LAN = Local Area Network, a network within a building or campus. Off-topic, moved to networks.

38.s: S. Ramanujan is the first Indian to be elected as Fellow of the following College:
38.x: In October 1918 Ramanujan became the first Indian elected a Fellow of Trinity College, Cambridge (he was also elected FRS that year).

38.s: Which port in Andhra Pradesh received the 'Golden Peacock Environment Management Award' in the year 2015 for its initiatives and achievement in the field of environment?
38.x: Krishnapatnam Port (Nellore) received the Golden Peacock Environment Management Award 2015 at the 17th World Congress on Environment Management, New Delhi (July 2015). (Awards item, moved.)

38.s: Which of the following organization is not associated with the organization of the "Sustainable Development Goals (SDG) Conclave 2020: Partnerships, Cooperation and Development of North Eastern States"?
38.src: Asst B.C Welfare Officers in AP B.C. Welfare Service, Royalt
38.x: The SDG Conclave 2020 (Guwahati, 24-26 Feb 2020) was organised by NITI Aayog with the North Eastern Council, Government of Assam, Tata Trusts, RIS and UNDP; the World Bank was not an organiser.

38.s: Which one of the following is not included in the world network of bio reserves?
38.src: Junior Asst. cum Typist in Prisons & Correctional Services 2
38.x: Manas BR (Assam) is not in UNESCO's World Network, while Nilgiri, Gulf of Mannar and Nanda Devi are.

38.s: Which of the following Biosphere reserve is included in the World network of Biosphere Reserves in 2016?
38.x: Agasthyamalai BR (Kerala–Tamil Nadu) was added to UNESCO's World Network in 2016. Nokrek and Simlipal joined in 2009 and Great Nicobar in 2013.

38.s: As of 2024 , how many Biosphere Reserves are there in India ?
38.src: APPSC 2025 Forest Beat Officer and Assistant Beat Officer In
38.x: India has 18 Biosphere Reserves (2024, unchanged in 2026), 13 of them in UNESCO's network.

38.s:
Match List‑I (Biosphere Reserves) with List‑II (States) and select the correct answer using the codes given below the Lists: List‑I (Biosphere Reserves)
A. Similipal
B. Dihang-Dibang
C. Nokrek
D. Kanchenjunga List‑II (States)
1. Sikkim
2. Uttaranchal
3. Arunachal Pradesh
4. Orissa
5. Meghalaya
Codes:
38.x: Similipal is in Odisha, Dihang-Dibang in Arunachal Pradesh, Nokrek in Meghalaya and Kanchenjunga in Sikkim, which gives A-4, B-3, C-5, D-1.

38.s: Bundala Biosphere Reserve which has been recently added to the UNESCO’s Man and Biosphere (MAB) network is located in ?
38.x: Bundala, a coastal wetland reserve added to UNESCO's MAB network (2005), is in Sri Lanka.

38.s: Where is Dibru Saikhowa Biosphere Reserve located?
38.x: Dibru-Saikhowa (NP and BR) is in Assam, bounded by the Brahmaputra, Lohit and Dibru rivers.

38.s: Arrange the following biosphere reserves in decreasing order of their geographical area:
38.x: By area, Nanda Devi (~5,860 km²) > Pachmarhi (~4,982) > Agasthyamalai (~3,500) > Panna.

38.s: The 16th Biosphere Reserve of India’ Cold Desert, lies in–
38.x: Cold Desert BR (2009), India's 16th, is in Himachal Pradesh (Lahaul-Spiti: Pin Valley NP, Kibber, Chandratal).

38.s: Which one of the following is not a Biosphere Reserve? Protected Area Network and Species PMF IAS E&E – 110
38.x: Nallamalai is a hill range, home of the Nagarjunasagar-Srisailam Tiger Reserve, not a Biosphere Reserve. Agasthyamalai, Nilgiri and Pachmarhi are BRs.

38.s: The most important strategy for the conservation of biodiversity, together with traditional human life, is the establishment of
38.x: Biosphere reserves combine conservation of biodiversity with the traditional life of local people. National parks and sanctuaries discourage human activity.

38.s: Which Biosphere Reserve harbours the highest number of animal species among Indian Biosphere Reserves, with 2,626 species?
38.x: The Sundarbans Biosphere Reserve harbours the highest number of animal species among Indian Biosphere Reserves, reported as 2,626.
38.tq: Match the largest species-count figure with the correct reserve rather than the largest area.
xs: **Sundarbans** has the most animal species of any Indian BR — **2,626** — option **(3)**.
**Great Rann of Kutch** is the **largest by area**; **Nilgiri** is the only three-state BR.
xa: Sundarbans BR (West Bengal) was designated **1989** and joined the WNBR in **2001**.
**Sundarbans NP** is a **World Heritage Site**.
**Nanda Devi** is known for **snow leopard, musk deer, blue sheep**.

38.s: The Citrus Gene Sanctuary in Nokrek Biosphere Reserve is an in-situ conservation site for which of the following?
38.x: The Citrus Gene Sanctuary in Nokrek Biosphere Reserve, Garo Hills, Meghalaya, conserves crop wild relatives in situ.
38.tq: Apply the meaning of a gene sanctuary to identify the resource conserved in its natural habitat.
xs: The **Citrus Gene Sanctuary** conserves **crop wild relatives** in situ — option **(1)**.
It lies in **Nokrek BR**, **Garo Hills, Meghalaya**.
xa: **Gene sanctuaries** are an **in-situ** method.
**Nokrek BR** was designated **1988** and joined the WNBR in **2009**.
**Field gene banks** (ex-situ) hold crops such as **mango, coconut, banana**.

38.s: Manas Biosphere Reserve is linked with which protected area?
38.x: Manas Biosphere Reserve is linked with the Manas Wildlife Sanctuary, not with Sundarbans National Park.

38.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the zonation of a biosphere reserve?
o: The core zone is legally protected, usually as a National Park or sanctuary
The transition zone permits settlements, agriculture, forestry and tourism
The buffer zone is the outer interface where settlements, farming and tourism are concentrated
The buffer zone allows regulated activities such as research, education and training
38.x: The buffer zone surrounds the core and allows only regulated activities; settlements, farming and tourism belong to the transition zone, the outer interface.
xa: **Seville Strategy (1995)** added social, cultural and economic needs and **community participation**.
Funding: **CSS "Biodiversity Conservation"** — **60:40**, and **90:10** for NE and Himalayan States.
UNESCO criteria include a **management authority** involving local communities.

38.s: Which of the following correctly describes the funding pattern for biosphere reserves?
o: 100 per cent central funding for all biosphere reserves
60:40 for the North-Eastern States, and 90:10 for all other States
90:10 for the North-Eastern and three Himalayan States, and 60:40 for other States
38.x: The funding pattern is 90:10 for the North-Eastern States and three Himalayan States, and 60:40 for other States.
38.tq: Compare the two funding ratios with the regional categories.
xs: BR funding: **90:10** for **North-Eastern and three Himalayan States**, **60:40** for others — option **(3)**.
Option (2) reverses the ratios.
Funding comes through the **CSS "Biodiversity Conservation"**, implemented by the **State Forest Department**.
xa: Umbrella scheme: **Conservation of Natural Resources and Ecosystems**.
**Integrated Management Plans**: five years, in four BRs, since **FY 2022-23**.
States prepare **Management Action Plans**; the **IN-MAB Committee** recommends sites.

38.s: Which of the following is NOT a criterion associated with UNESCO's Biosphere Reserve framework?
o: A management authority involving local or tribal communities
Viable populations representing all trophic levels in the core
An effectively protected and minimally disturbed core
Compulsory transfer of land ownership to UNESCO
38.x: UNESCO's criteria include a protected core, viable populations across trophic levels and participatory management. Transfer of land ownership to UNESCO is not a criterion.
38.tq: Find the option that confuses international designation with ownership or administration.
xs: **Compulsory transfer of land ownership to UNESCO** is not a BR criterion — option **(4)**.
A BR **does not change legal status or ownership** of land.
Real criteria: a **minimally disturbed core** with **all trophic levels**, and a **management authority** involving local communities.
xa: The **Seville Strategy (1995)** added social, cultural, economic needs and **community participation**.
BRs are designated under UNESCO's **MAB Programme** (**1971**).
BRs are **nominated by national governments**.

38.s: Which organisation launched the Man and the Biosphere (MAB) Programme in 1971, under which Biosphere Reserves are designated?
38.x: The MAB Programme, launched in 1971, is a UNESCO programme, and Biosphere Reserves were started by UNESCO, not IUCN. IUCN deals with the Red List and PA categories, UNEP with the environment programme and WDPA (via UNEP-WCMC), and WWF is an NGO.
38.tq: MAB = UNESCO, 1971.
xs: The **MAB Programme** (launched **1971**) is a **UNESCO** programme — option **(3)**.
BRs were started by **UNESCO, not IUCN**.
**UNEP** runs the **WDPA** through **UNEP-WCMC**; **WWF** publishes the Living Planet Report.
xa: ⚠ Some keys give **1972** (RPSC 2013) or **1973-74**.
India's first BR: **Nilgiri (1986)**; first Indian entry in the WNBR (**2000**).
**13** of India's **18** BRs are in UNESCO's **WNBR**.

38.s: Which Biosphere Reserve, including Lahaul-Spiti, is India's first high-altitude cold desert site in UNESCO's World Network?
38.x: The Cold Desert Biosphere Reserve in Lahaul-Spiti (Pin Valley NP, Kibber WLS, Chandratal) is India's first high-altitude cold desert site in the WNBR.
xa: It also covers **Pin Valley NP**, **Kibber WLS** and **Chandratal**; flagship animal **snow leopard**.
It joined the WNBR in **September 2025** at Hangzhou.
⚠ PYQmarked Cold Desert as not in MAB — true then.

38.s: Of India's 18 Biosphere Reserves, how many are included in UNESCO's World Network of Biosphere Reserves?
38.x: 13 of India's 18 Biosphere Reserves are in UNESCO's World Network of Biosphere Reserves.
xa: The **18 BRs** cover about **91,425.11 sq km**.
Outside the WNBR: **Manas**, **Dibru-Saikhowa**, **Dehang-Dibang**, **Great Rann of Kutch**, **Seshachalam**.
⚠ "All Indian BRs are in the UNESCO network" — false (**13 of 18**).

38.s: Which Indian Biosphere Reserve was included in UNESCO's World Network of Biosphere Reserves in 2016?
38.x: Agasthyamalai entered the World Network in 2016. Seshachalam, Manas and Dibru-Saikhowa are among the five not yet included.

38.s: Which was the first Biosphere Reserve established in India?

Thermal expansion of seawater and melting of glaciers and ice sheets

52.s: Which statement about tropical cyclones and marine heatwaves is correct?

Cyclones are more frequent in the **Bay of Bengal** than the Arabian Sea.

AP cyclones peak **October-December**.

52.s: Which one of the following provides the cryogenic indicator of climate change?
52.x: An ice core, drilled from an ice sheet or glacier, is the cryogenic indicator: its layers and trapped air record past climate. Pollen, tree rings and evaporites are biological or sedimentary proxies.

52.s: Which of the following is a potential tipping point of global climate change?

52.s:
Assertion (A): The 1.2°C threshold for large-scale collapse of warm-water coral reefs has already been crossed.

o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

52.s: What is a climate tipping point?
o: global temperatures immediately return to pre-industrial levels
only short-term weather changes occur without wider consequences
climate variations become completely predictable and reversible
small changes can trigger large, self-perpetuating and potentially irreversible shifts
52.x: A tipping point is a threshold beyond which small changes may produce large, self-perpetuating and irreversible shifts in a non-linear system.
52.tq: Apply the definition to distinguish a non-linear threshold from ordinary climate variability.
xs: A tipping point is where **small changes trigger large, self-perpetuating, irreversible shifts** — option **(4)**.
Behaviour is **non-linear**, so options (1)-(3) are wrong.
xa: **Coral reefs** have already crossed the **1.2 C** threshold.
Beyond ~**2 C**, parts of the **Amazon** may become savanna.

52.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Amazon rainforest?
o: About 17-18% of the Amazon has already been lost
Beyond about 2°C of warming, parts may turn from a carbon source into a carbon store
The Amazon makes about 50% of its own rain
Beyond about 2°C of warming, parts may turn into savanna
52.x: Beyond about 2°C parts may flip from carbon store to carbon source, the reverse of what is stated.
xa: Parts may become **savanna**.
⚠ Coral threshold **1.2 C** already crossed; Amazon risk beyond ~**2 C**.

52.s: Which one of the following is a climate tipping element that is currently near record lows?
52.x: Arctic sea ice is a recognised climate tipping element and is near record lows (APPSC-G2 2025 answer). Desert dunes, the Deccan basalts and European temperate deciduous forests are not among the tipping elements scientists list (which include warm-water coral reefs, the Amazon, Greenland and West Antarctic ice sheets, AMOC and permafrost).
52.tq: Tipping elements: Arctic sea ice, coral reefs, Amazon, ice sheets, AMOC, permafrost.
xs: **Arctic sea ice** is the tipping element near record lows — option **(1)** (**APPSC-G2 2025** answer).
Desert dunes, Deccan basalts and European deciduous forests are not among the tipping elements listed.
xa: Ice-free Arctic summer: **once a century** at **1.5 C** vs **once a decade** at **2 C** (IPCC SR1.5, 2018).
Other tipping elements: **Greenland and West Antarctic ice sheets**, **AMOC**, **permafrost**, the **Amazon**.
**Warm-water coral reefs** are the most fragile: the **1.2 C** threshold is already crossed.
A **tipping point** triggers **self-perpetuating, irreversible**, **non-linear** shifts.

55.s: The United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change deals with
55.x: The UNFCCC's objective is to stabilise greenhouse-gas concentrations, i.e. mitigation of all GHG emissions. That is wider than cutting fossil fuels or CO₂ alone, and uranium is irrelevant.

55.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the UNFCCC?
o: It was adopted on 9 May 1992 at New York

Hydrogen produces zero carbon emissions when burned or used in fuel cells. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #9 · pp 33-36]
Hydrogen produces only water vapour when burned or used in fuel cells. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #9 · pp 33-36]

CNG and LPG are cleaner than petrol and diesel. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #9 · pp 33-36]
CNG and LPG produce lower CO, unburnt hydrocarbons, and particulate emissions than petrol and diesel. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #9 · pp 33-36]
CNG is a cleaner alternative to petrol and diesel. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #9 · pp 33-36]

43.s: Photochemical smog is a resultant of the reaction among
o: NO₂, 03 and peroxyacetyl nitrate in the presence of sunlight
CO, 02 and peroxyacetyl nitrate in the presence of sunlight
CO, CO₂ and N02 at low temperature
High concentration of N02, O₃ and CO in the evening

43.x: Ozone (with PAN) is produced during photochemical smog formation; hydrocarbons and nitrogen oxides are the inputs, not products.

43.x: Smog is essentially caused by oxides of nitrogen (photochemical smog) and sulphur (classical smog); oxygen and nitrogen are normal air gases.

o: Los Angeles and warm, sunny conditions
Los Angeles and cold, humid conditions
43.x: Photochemical smog is linked with Los Angeles and warm, sunny weather; classical smog with London and cold, humid weather.
xa: ⚠ Trap: **London** smog = cold + **SO2**; **Los Angeles** smog = warm + **sunlight**.
**Photochemical smog** is itself listed as a **secondary pollutant**.
**Asian Brown Cloud**: soot + **black carbon** + aerosols over South Asia and the Indian Ocean in the **dry season**.

43.s: What is the Asian Brown Cloud?
o: A layer of soot, black carbon and aerosols over South Asia and the Indian Ocean during the dry season
A permanent ozone layer over the Himalayan region
A layer of volcanic ash restricted to Europe
A seasonal band of water vapour over the Pacific Ocean
43.x: The Asian Brown Cloud is a dry-season layer of soot, black carbon and aerosols over South Asia and the Indian Ocean, arising mainly from biomass and fossil-fuel burning.
43.tq: Identify the phenomenon from its composition, region and season together.
xs: The **Asian Brown Cloud** is soot, **black carbon** and aerosols over **South Asia and the Indian Ocean** in the **dry season** — so option **(1)** is correct.
It comes from **biomass and fossil-fuel burning**, not from volcanic ash, ozone or water vapour.
xa: **Photochemical smog** (Los Angeles) = NOx + VOCs + sunlight → **ozone, PAN**.
**Classical smog** (London) = **SO2**, smoke, particulates + fog in cold, humid conditions.
**Biomass burning** is also listed among **anthropogenic** sources of air pollution.

43.s: Photochemical smog forms when sunlight drives reactions between hydrocarbons and which gases?
43.x: Sunlight makes nitrogen oxides and hydrocarbons from vehicles react into ozone and PAN, forming photochemical smog.
n: Photochemical smog is formed from nitrogen oxides, hydrocarbons and sunlight. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 21-23]

43.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Ground-level ozone — direct emission from coal mines
43.x: Ground-level ozone is formed from nitrogen oxides and volatile organic compounds in sunlight; it is not directly emitted from coal mines. Ammonia, hydrogen sulphide and magnetite particles have the listed sources.
43.tq: Reject the option that assigns a secondary pollutant a direct source unrelated to its formation process.
xs: **Ground-level ozone — direct emission from coal mines** is wrong — so option **(3)** is correct.
Ground-level ozone is **secondary**: formed from **NOx + VOCs in sunlight**.
The other pairs are right: **H2S** ← sewage, refineries; **magnetite** ← vehicle brake wear; **ammonia** ← fertilisers and livestock.
xa: Ozone effects: **asthma**, eye irritation and **crop damage**.
Ozone was included in **NAAQS** for the first time in the **2009** revision.
**PAN** is the other secondary product of photochemical smog.

43.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Vehicles — Ammonium sulphate emitted directly in final form
43.x: Vehicles emit pollutants such as carbon monoxide, nitrogen oxides, VOCs, particulate matter and unburnt hydrocarbons. Ammonium sulphate is formed secondarily in the atmosphere.
43.tq: Find the option that confuses a directly emitted pollutant with a secondary pollutant.
xs: **Vehicles — ammonium sulphate emitted directly** is the wrong pair — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Ammonium sulphate** is a **secondary** product formed in the air from **SO2 + NH3**; vehicles emit **CO, NOx, VOCs, PM**, hydrocarbons and lead.
The other pairs are right: agriculture → **ammonia, methane**; **coal-fired power plants** and **metal-ore smelting** → **SO2**.
xa: Ammonium sulphate makes up nearly **1/3 of India's PM2.5**; **ammonium nitrate** up to **50%**.
**Primary pollutants** (emitted directly): **CO, SO2, NOx, PM, lead**.
**Secondary pollutants**: **O3, PAN**, photochemical smog, ammonium sulphate, ammonium nitrate.

43.s: Which of the following is a primary pollutant?
43.x: Lead from vehicles is emitted directly; ozone, PAN and ammonium sulphate form in the atmosphere.
xa: Primary pollutants: **CO, SO2, NOx (NO), PM, lead**.
**Ammonium nitrate** is also secondary → up to **50%** of India's PM2.5.
**Lead** from motor vehicles and smelters causes **brain damage**.

o: Warm, sunny weather with NOx and VOCs

43.s:
What is true about gaseous pollutants?

I. In humans, Sulphur Dioxide pollution causes headache, vomiting, irritation of eye and respiratory passages.

II. Nitrogen oxides are one source of photochemical smog, acid deposition and ozone depletion.

III. Mild Carbon Mono Oxide poisoning causes lung disorders like necrosis and emphysema.

xs: The **rotten-egg smell** is due to **hydrogen sulphide (H2S)** — so option **(3)** is correct.

**CO** reduces the blood's oxygen-carrying capacity; **SO2** comes from burning coal/oil; **ammonia** comes from fertilisers and livestock.

45.s: How can improper waste management, especially biomedical and e-waste, indirectly contribute to deforestation and biodiversity loss?

By reducing industrial pollution and improving ecosystem balance
By increasing green cover through waste-to-energy plants in forests

45.s:

45.s: The Andhra Pradesh Pollution Control Board was set up in 1976 under which law?
o: Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974
Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1981
45.x: APPCB was set up in 1976 under the Water Act, 1974. The Air Act (1981), the Environment (Protection) Act (1986) and the Noise Rules (2000) came after 1976, so APPCB could not have been created under them.
xs: **APPCB** was set up in **1976** under the **Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974**, so option **(1)** is correct.
The **Air Act (1981)**, **EPA (1986)** and **Noise Rules (2000)** all came after 1976.
xa: APPCB runs **25 Real Time Noise Monitoring Stations** and **9 CETPs**.
It pushes **Zero Liquid Discharge**.

45.s: What is the build-up of toxic chemicals or radioactive material in soil called?
45.x: Soil pollution is the build-up of toxic chemicals or radioactive material in soil; it causes toxic crops and reduces vegetation.
xa: Other effects: **clogged drains**, **foul smell**.
Main primary source of soil pollution = **chemical fertilisers and pesticides** (**APPSC-G2 2025**).
Constitutional link: **Art. 48A**; SDG **2, 15**.

45.s: With which sources is mercury pollution mainly associated?
45.x: Mercury is associated with chlor-alkali effluent and fungicides; chromates with tanneries, cadmium with phosphate fertilisers and batteries.
xa: ⚠ **Mercury** → **Minamata**; **cadmium** → **itai-itai**.
**DDT** is a **persistent organic pollutant** that **biomagnifies**.
Chemically contaminated sites are tested against **189 hazardous chemicals**.

45.s: Which of the following diseases is associated with mercury pollution?
45.x: Mercury pollution is associated with Minamata disease, whereas cadmium pollution is associated with itai-itai disease.
45.tq: Discriminate between the two heavy-metal disease associations.
xs: Mercury pollution causes **Minamata disease**, so option **(2)** is correct.
**Itai-itai** is caused by **cadmium**.
xa: Mercury comes from **chlor-alkali** effluent and fungicides.
**DDT and mercury** biomagnify in marine food chains.
Cadmium sources: **mining effluent**, **phosphate fertilisers**, **batteries**.

45.s: DDT, a persistent organic pollutant, is listed under which convention?
45.x: DDT is a persistent organic pollutant listed under the Stockholm Convention.
xa: DDT, **aldrin** and **malathion** are pesticide soil polluters.
**DDT and mercury** biomagnify in **marine** food chains.
Control: less chemical pesticide, **biofertilisers and IPM**, **organic farming**.

45.s: Under the Contaminated Sites Rules, sites are tested against how many hazardous chemicals?
45.x: The Rules, made under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986, test sites against 189 hazardous chemicals.
xa: The Rules aim to **identify + remediate** chemically contaminated sites (**Jun 2026**).
**Environment (Protection) Fund Rules**: money usable for site remediation; **25%** kept by the Centre.
**Fly ash** must be used within **300 km** of thermal plants.

45.s: Which one of the following is NOT a measure for controlling soil pollution?

xs: **Watersheds** are not a soil-pollution control, so option **(2)** is correct (**APPSC 2019** trap).
**Crop rotation**, **biofertilisers** and **IPM** are listed controls.
xa: Other controls: **afforestation**, **organic farming**, **biomining** of legacy dumps.
**Fly ash** must go into **bricks, cement and roads**, not onto soil.
⚠ **Incineration** is conventional → NOT an alternative (**APPSC-G2 2025**).

45.s: Fly ash from thermal power plants must be used in bricks, cement and roads within what distance of the plant?
45.x: Fly ash must be used in bricks, cement and roads within 300 km of thermal plants; 50 km is the limit for using treated STP wastewater.
xa: **Coal ash** is a human cause of soil pollution.
**Contaminated Sites Rules** test against **189 hazardous chemicals**.
**Polluter Pays** applies under the Contaminated Sites Rules.

45.s: Which of the following pairs (substance – behaviour in marine food chains) is correctly matched?
45.x: DDT and mercury biomagnify through marine food chains; dissolved oxygen is not a pollutant and does not biomagnify.

45.s: The Noise Pollution (Regulation and Control) Rules, 2000 were framed under which enactment?
o: The Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974
The Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1981

45.s: What is the primary application of bioremediation?
45.x: Bioremediation is used mainly to clean contaminated soil (and groundwater), using microbes or plants to break down oil, pesticides and solvents. It is not a tool for noise, air or waterborne disease.

45.s: What is adding nutrients to boost native microbes at a contaminated site called?
45.x: Biostimulation adds nutrients to boost native microbes; bioaugmentation adds pollutant-degrading microbes.

o: Fungi such as the oyster mushroom

45.s: What is adding pollutant-degrading microbes to a contaminated site called?
45.x: Bioaugmentation adds pollutant-degrading microbes; biostimulation only adds nutrients to boost native microbes.

45.x: Incineration is itself a conventional method; green technology, bioremediation and CCS are the alternatives.

I. Food processing units produce gypsum

II. Thermal power plants produce biodegradable wastes
42.x: Both statements are wrong. Gypsum comes from fertiliser plants, not food processing, and thermal power plants produce fly ash, which is non-biodegradable.

42.s:
Which of the following statements is correct regarding sanitary landfills ?

I. It was adopted as the substitute to open-burning dumps

II. In a sanitary landfill, wastes are dumped in a depression or trench after compaction, and covered with dirt everyday.
42.x: Both are correct. Sanitary landfills were adopted as substitutes for open-burning dumps, and in them waste is compacted in a trench or depression and covered with earth every day.

42.s: Following statement is not true for plastic waste
o: Can be used to make compost
42.src: Grama Ward Sachivalayam Category-III Ward Sanitation Secreta
42.x: Plastic waste cannot be composted, so statement B is the untrue one. It does give toxic fumes when burnt and it lasts long, so 'all of the above' is wrong.

42.s: Which of the following is a better method to reduce the problem of solid waste?
42.x: Recycling is the better method because it turns waste into usable material and cuts the amount left for disposal. Burning in landfills, sea dumping and compressing only move or concentrate the problem.

42.s: In March 2025, which of the following directives was issued by the Andhra Pradesh Pollution Control Board (APPCB) to reduce coal consumption and manage solid waste in the cement industry?
o: Mandating the use of Refuse-Derived Fuel (RDF) in cement kilns
Implementing a ban on plastic packaging in cement products
Requiring all cement plants to relocate outside urban areas
Introducing a carbon tax on cement production emissions
42.src: APPSC 2023 Lecturers in Government Degree Colleges
42.x: In March 2025 the APPCB told cement plants to use Refuse-Derived Fuel in their kilns, under the SWM Rules, to cut coal use and dispose of solid waste. The other options are not directives it issued.

42.s:
Match the following:
Waste Disposal Method a. Landfilling b. Incineration c. Composting d. Recycling
Pros/Cons I. Low-cost, but has long-term environmental impact II. Reduces volume of waste, but emits pollutants III. Produces useful by-products like biogas, but requires land IV. Conserves resources, but needs infrastructure
42.x: Landfill is cheap but harms the environment in the long term, incineration cuts volume but emits pollutants, composting gives useful by-products but needs land, and recycling saves resources but needs infrastructure. That gives a-I, b-II, c-III, d-IV.

42.s: In the context of which one of the following arcs the terms 'pyrolysis and plasma gasification' mentioned?
42.x: Pyrolysis (heating waste without oxygen) and plasma gasification (extreme heat that turns organics into syngas) are waste-to-energy technologies, not rare-earth, natural-gas or hydrogen-vehicle technologies.

42.s: Which of the following statement is incorrect in reference to compost?
o: In this, biodegradable waste is decomposed in pits
It is rich in organic matter and nutrients
The process of decomposition in pits is slowed down
The waste material decomposed is farm waste material
42.x: Statement (c) is wrong: in compost pits earthworms and microbes speed up decomposition, they do not slow it down. Biodegradable farm waste decomposed in pits gives compost rich in organic matter and nutrients.

42.s: Incinerators are used for which of the following?
42.x: Incinerators are furnaces for burning waste at high temperature under control. They are not used to store waste, cut trees or make fertiliser.

42.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about sanitary landfills?
o: Waste is compacted in cells and covered with earth daily.
The method relies mainly on containment rather than treatment.
Liners and leachate-collection systems are used.
They are intended for all biodegradable waste without segregation.
42.x: Sanitary landfills are not meant for all biodegradable waste without segregation; the other features are correct.
xa: Sanitary landfill is the **most common and economic** method; it includes **methane and groundwater monitoring**.

42.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about waste-to-energy technologies?
o: Incineration burns waste in the absence of oxygen.
Incineration can reduce waste volume by about 90 per cent.
Incineration may generate ash and emissions.
Biomethanation converts wet organic waste into biogas through microbial action.
42.x: Incineration burns waste in oxygen (and may produce steam for power); it does not work in the absence of oxygen.
xa: India (Feb 2026): **21 operational WtE plants** producing **170+ MW** + **133 biogas facilities**.
AP WtE plants: **Guntur** and **Visakhapatnam**.
SBM-U 2.0 target: **10,000 TPD** additional WtE capacity.

42.s: In which of the following is Refuse-Derived Fuel (RDF) mainly used as an alternative fuel?
o: Cement kilns and thermal power plants
42.x: RDF, made by shredding and dehydrating high-calorific MSW, is used in cement kilns and thermal power plants.
xa: Non-recyclable high-calorific dry waste goes to **RDF / co-processing in cement kilns**.
**WtE** cuts MSW volume by **~90%**.
**Biomedical waste** goes for incineration at a **CBMWTF**; **broken glass** to landfilling.

42.s: Which of the following describes the Indore method of composting?
o: Anaerobic pits with alternate layers of solid waste and night soil
Aerobic composting with the waste turned at intervals
42.x: The Indore method is aerobic composting with turning at intervals; anaerobic pits with layers of MSW and night soil are the Bangalore method.

42.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes incineration from pyrolysis?
o: Incineration heats waste in the absence of oxygen, whereas pyrolysis uses excess oxygen
Incineration is controlled high-temperature burning, whereas pyrolysis heats waste without oxygen
Both methods are biological processes using earthworms
Both methods are restricted to inert waste in sanitary landfills
42.x: Incineration is controlled high-temperature combustion, while pyrolysis is thermal treatment in the absence of oxygen.
42.tq: Compare the defining operating condition of two similar thermal technologies.
xs: **Incineration** is controlled **high-temperature burning**; **pyrolysis** heats waste **without oxygen** — option **(2)** is correct.
Option (1) reverses them; **earthworms** belong to vermicomposting; **inert waste** goes to sanitary landfill.
xa: Incineration cuts volume **up to 90%**, recovers energy as steam, but causes **air pollution** and ash disposal problems.
Pyrolysis gives **gas, oil, char**; it suits mixed/contaminated streams but is **costly**.
Incineration suits **hazardous, biomedical, combustible** waste.

42.s: Which of the following pairs (waste – preferred method) is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Biomedical waste – Incineration at a common treatment facility
42.x: High-calorific dry waste is used as RDF or co-processed in cement kilns, not landfilled.
xa: APPSC-G2 2023 match: organic → **composting**, e-waste → recycling, hazardous → **incineration**, glass → landfilling.
**RDF** is made by **shredding and dehydrating** high-calorific MSW; used in **cement kilns** and thermal power plants.
AP: **APPCB** permitted **12 cement industries** to co-process waste.

42.s: In hazardous-waste disposal, which option is treated as the last resort?
42.x: Landfill is the last resort; APPCB prefers co-processing as fuel in cement plants and waste exchange between industries.

42.s: With the help of which organisms is vermicompost produced?
42.x: Vermicompost is made by earthworms, which makes vermicomposting a biological method of composting.

Recycling is the processing of waste into usable material. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #26 · pp 45-47]

42.s: Which alternative method is associated with oil spills and oily sludge?
42.x: Oilzapper, a mix of bacteria, cleans up oil spills and oily sludge. A microbial fuel cell treats wastewater, and EPR is a producer duty.
42.tq: Match each method to its use.
n: Oilzapper addresses oil spills and oily sludge. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 70-71]
MFC addresses wastewater and electricity generation. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 70-71]
Composting processes biodegradable waste. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 70-71]
EPR assigns producers end-of-life responsibility. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 70-71]
xs: **Oilzapper** addresses **oil spills** and **oily sludge** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**MFC** addresses **wastewater** and **electricity generation**; **EPR** assigns **producers** end-of-life responsibility.
**Composting** treats **biodegradable waste**.
xa: **Bioremediation** uses **microorganisms** for **pollutant removal**, incl. oil spills.
**Genetically engineered microbes** target **specific pollutants**.
**UV purification** targets **microorganisms** in **water**.

o: Bioremediation – Using naturally occurring organisms to remove pollutants
UV purification – Thermal breakdown of waste without oxygen
Pyrolysis – Thermal breakdown of waste without oxygen to recover energy
42.x: UV purification kills microorganisms in drinking water; thermal breakdown without oxygen is pyrolysis.
n: Bioremediation addresses toxic pollutants and oil spills. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 70-71]

42.s: Hydrogen is regarded as a clean fuel because hydrogen fuel cells emit only which of the following?
42.x: Hydrogen fuel cells emit only water vapour, which is why hydrogen is considered a clean fuel.

Biofuels are an alternative to fossil fuels. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 70-71]

42.s: For what purpose is biomedical waste in Andhra Pradesh mainly sent to Common Bio-Medical Waste Treatment Facilities?
o: Production of RDF for cement kilns only

Open dumping and untreated composting are not permitted routes.
xa: **Yellow** category BMW → incineration / **plasma pyrolysis** / deep burial.
BMW Rules 2016 use **barcoding and GPS tracking**.
India (2024): **1.89 lakh** facilities generate **800+ tonnes/day**.

42.s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: Landfill is associated with solid waste disposal.
EPR refers to the producer's end-of-life responsibility.
R2 refers to wastewater treatment and electricity generation.
42.x: Option C is incorrect: R2 is about responsible electronics recycling. Wastewater treatment with electricity is the microbial fuel cell.
42.tq: Match each waste term to its meaning.
n: A landfill is used for solid-waste disposal. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #39 · pp 68-70]
Extended Producer Responsibility assigns producers responsibility for end-of-life management. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #39 · pp 68-70]
R2 is associated with electronics recycling. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #39 · pp 68-70]
Compost is decomposed biodegradable waste. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #39 · pp 68-70]
MFCs are associated with wastewater treatment and electricity generation. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #39 · pp 68-70]
xs: The incorrect statement is that **R2** refers to **wastewater treatment and electricity generation** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**R2** relates to the **electronics recycling industry** — **responsible electronics recycling**.
**Wastewater** and **electricity generation** is the **MFC**.
xa: A company following the **R2 Code of Practices** can become **R2 Certified** (UPSC **2021**).
**78%** of e-waste is processed informally; hubs at **Seelampur** and **Moradabad**.

42.s: Which method of solid-waste disposal is described as not viable in urban India?
42.x: Composting, incineration and landfilling are all used in urban India; only uncontrolled dumping is described as not viable.
xa: **Composting** = aerobic, for biodegradable organic/wet waste; **incineration** suits hazardous, biomedical, combustible waste.
**Sanitary landfill** is the most common and economic method, for **residual** waste only.
Incineration cuts volume **up to 90%** but causes air pollution and ash disposal problems.

42.s: Which of the following is compost?
o: Disposal of solid waste in a designated land area
Decomposed organic waste that becomes nutrient-rich material
42.x: Compost is organic waste that has broken down into nutrient-rich material. The other options describe landfill, recycling and incineration.

n: Compost is decomposed organic waste. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #26 · pp 45-47]
Compost is a nutrient-rich material. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #26 · pp 45-47]

Incineration is the controlled burning of waste. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #26 · pp 45-47]
Recycling is the processing of waste into usable material. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #26 · pp 45-47]
Compost contains organic matter. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #26 · pp 45-47]
Compost contains nutrients. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #26 · pp 45-47]
xs: **Compost** is **decomposed** organic waste that becomes **nutrient-rich material** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Disposal in a designated land area** is a **landfill**; **processing waste into usable material** is **recycling**.
**Controlled burning** of waste is **incineration**.
xa: **Indore method** = aerobic composting with turning at intervals.
⚠ **Bangalore method** = anaerobic pit composting, **4-6 months**.
**Vermicompost** is produced using **earthworms**.

42.s: The Solid Waste Management Rules, 2016, replaced which earlier set of rules?
42.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening
42.x:
the SWM Rules 2016 have themselves been replaced — now the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026 (in force 1 April 2026, four-stream segregation) (PMF Lens Feb 2026 p.5)
The Solid Waste Management Rules 2016 replaced the Municipal Solid Wastes (Management and Handling) Rules, 2000. The other rules had their own successors.

42.s: An RDBMS consists of
42.x: An RDBMS stores data as a collection of related tables (relations) made of records and fields. (Moved to 5:12.)

42.s: Which of the following is the primary goal of India's "Municipal Solid Waste Management and Handling Rules, 2000"?
42.x: The MSW (Management and Handling) Rules 2000 made urban local bodies collect, segregate, store, transport, process and dispose of waste, with segregation as a foundational aim.

42.s: As per the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2016 in India, which one of the following statements is correct?
o: Waste generator has to segregate waste into five categories.
The Rules are applicable to notified urban local bodies, notified towns and all industrial townships only.
The Rules provide for exact and elaborate criteria for the identification of sites for landfills and waste processing
It is mandatory on the part of the waste generator that the waste generated in one district cannot be moved to another
42.x:
the SWM Rules 2016 were replaced by the SWM Rules, 2026 (in force 1 April 2026), which require four streams — wet, dry, sanitary, special care (PMF Lens Feb 2026 p.5)
The SWM Rules 2016 set exact criteria for siting landfills and waste-processing facilities (e.g. 100 m from a river, 20 km from airports). Segregation was into 3 streams (not five), the rules went beyond ULBs and industrial townships, and there is no ban on moving waste between districts.

42.s: Which one of the following is known for cleaning a polluted environment?
42.x: Rain washes particles and soluble gases out of the air (wet deposition), so it cleans a polluted atmosphere. (Moved to 5:99.)

42.s: Which of the following was a provision of the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2016?
o: Unrestricted disposal of untreated waste in landfills
Exemption of brand owners from waste responsibility
Extended producer responsibility for producers and brand owners
42.x: The 2016 Rules provided for user fees, spot fines and EPR for producers and brand owners, and prohibited untreated waste in landfills.
xa: The 2016 Rules came into force on **8 Apr 2016**, replacing the **2000** Rules.
They extended to **UAs, census towns, railways, airports, SEZs**, religious/historical places.
**EPR** first entered Indian law via the **E-waste (M&H) Rules 2011**.

42.s: Under the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026, what must a Bulk Waste Generator do?
o: Send all its wet waste to a landfill
Hand over unsegregated waste to the Urban Local Body
Process wet waste on site or obtain an EBWGR certificate
Mix sanitary waste with dry recyclable waste
42.x: Bulk Waste Generators must process wet waste on site or obtain an EBWGR certificate under the 2026 Rules.
xa: Every generator: four-stream segregation — **wet, dry, sanitary, special care**.
Hill/island bodies: **user fee on tourists**; regulate tourist inflow.
Local bodies: map legacy dumpsites; **biomining**.

42.s: Environmental Compensation under the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026 follows which principle?
42.x: Environmental Compensation follows the polluter-pays principle, not the precautionary principle.

42.s: Under the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2016, used diapers and sanitary napkins were generally to be wrapped and placed in which stream?
42.x: Under the 2016 system, used diapers and sanitary napkins were generally wrapped and placed in the dry bin. The 2026 Rules provide a separate sanitary stream.
42.tq: Discriminate between the earlier three-stream rule and the later four-stream rule.
xs: Under the **SWM Rules 2016**, used diapers and sanitary napkins went wrapped into the **dry waste** bin — option **(3)** is correct.
A separate **sanitary** stream came only with the **SWM Rules 2026**.
xa: ⚠ Some notes put diapers/napkins under **domestic hazardous** (2016).
2016 streams: **biodegradable (wet), dry, domestic hazardous**.
2026 streams: **wet, dry, sanitary, special care**.

42.s: Under the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026, paper, plastics and metals go into which bin?
42.x: Paper, plastics and metals go in the dry bin; wet waste covers food scraps, peels and garden waste.

42.s: What did the Supreme Court hold in its order of 18 August 2026 on responsibility for waste at the threshold?
o: Only Urban Local Bodies are responsible for such waste
Only sanitary workers are responsible for such waste
Responsibility begins only after waste reaches a landfill
Generators, and not only sanitary workers, are responsible for such waste

xs: The SC order of **18 Aug 2026** held that **generators**, not only sanitary workers, are responsible for waste at the threshold — option **(4)** is correct.

xa: SC pulled up Union and States for not institutionalising **SWM Rules 2026** (**1 Sep 2026**).
SC earlier gave pan-India directions; clean environment part of **Art. 21** (Feb 2026).

42.x: Plastic pollution is the build-up of non-biodegradable plastic waste in the oceans that threatens marine life. Acid rain, desertification and eutrophication are other problems.

42.s: Which is the first country to completely ban disposable plastic cups, plates and other plastic utensils?
42.x: France was the first country to ban disposable plastic cups, plates and cutlery (law of 2016, in force 2020).

42.s: In August 2021, the Plastic Waste Management Amendment Rules, 2021, was notified by the Government of India, which is aimed at phasing-out single use plastic by ______.
42.x: The PWM Amendment Rules of 12 Aug 2021 aimed to phase out identified single-use plastic items by 2022 (ban from 1 July 2022).

42.s: Bisphenol A (BPA), a cause of concern, is a structural/key component in the manufacture of which of the following kinds of plastics?
42.x: Bisphenol A is a key building block of polycarbonate plastics (and epoxy resins) and leaches from them. LDPE, PET and PVC are not made from BPA.

42.s:
Consider the following :
I. Cigarette butts
II. Eyeglass lenses
III. Car tyres
How many of them contain plastic?
42.x: All three contain plastic: cigarette filters are cellulose acetate, most eyeglass lenses are plastic polymers, and car tyres contain synthetic rubber polymers.

42.s: Bisphenol A (BPA), a cause of concern, is a structural/ key component in the manufacture of which of the following kinds of plastics?
42.x: Bisphenol A is a key building block of polycarbonate plastics (and epoxy resins) and leaches from them. LDPE, PET and PVC are not made from BPA.

42.s:
Which of the following statements about India's largest Charkha is/are true?
1. It was inaugurated in Noida.
2. It is made of used plastic waste.
Select the correct answer from codes given below :
42.x: Both are true: India's largest charkha, made of used plastic waste, was inaugurated in Noida on the eve of Gandhi's 150th birth anniversary (2019).

42.s: Under the Plastic Waste Management (Amendment) Rules, 2026, for up to how long may unmet targets be carried forward?
42.x: The 2026 amendment allows unmet targets to be carried forward for up to three years, not five.

42.s: Microbeads are prohibited under the Plastic Waste Management Rules in which products?
42.x: The PWM Rules ban microbeads in cosmetics; separately, an FSSAI study found microplastics in all tested sugar and salt samples.

42.s: Which of the following was issued by the CPCB in response to biomedical waste generated during the COVID-19 period?
o: Global E-waste Monitor and Basel Protocol
R2 electronics recycling code and plastic treaty guidelines
COVID19BWM tracking app and COVID-19 waste guidelines
42.x: The CPCB issued COVID-19 biomedical-waste guidelines in 2020 and introduced the COVID19BWM tracking app.
42.tq: Match the emergency, authority and digital tracking instrument.
xs: **CPCB** issued **COVID-19 waste guidelines** in **2020** and the **COVID19BWM** tracking app — option **(3)** is correct.
**Global E-waste Monitor** is by ITU/UNITAR; **R2** is an e-waste certification; **Swachh App** is Guntur's plastic-fine tool.
xa: BMW Rules 2016 use **barcoding and GPS tracking**.

42.s: Which of the following pairs (resin code – plastic) is correctly matched?
42.x: Resin code 1 is PET, 2 is HDPE, 3 is PVC and 5 is PP.
xa: Others: **4 LDPE**, **6 PS**, **7 others** incl. **polycarbonate** (BPA).
**PET** — water and soft-drink bottles; **LDPE/HDPE** — carry bags, milk bottles.
**Rigid** plastics (PET, HDPE bottles) need **30% → 60%** recycled content by 2028-29.

42.s: What is the minimum thickness of plastic carry bags in India from 31 December 2022?
42.x: Thickness rose from 40 (2011) to 50 (2016), 75 (30 September 2021) and 120 microns (31 December 2022).
xa: The **75** and **120 micron** steps came from the **PWM Amendment Rules 2021** (12 Aug 2021, GSR 571(E)).
**PWM Rules 2016** also brought **50-micron packaging sheets**, a PWM fee on retailers and **plastic roads**.
AP bans SUP and carry bags **under 120 microns**.

42.s: On which date did India's ban on identified single-use plastic items come into force?
42.x: The SUP ban took effect on 1 July 2022; the EPR Guidelines on plastic packaging also became effective in July 2022.
xa: **PWM Amendment Rules 2021** aimed to phase out SUP by **2022**.
The SUP ban covers only **11%** of total plastic waste (CSE **2023**).

42.s: Under the Plastic Waste Management Amendment Rules, 2024, from which body do makers of biodegradable plastics need certification?
o: Food Safety and Standards Authority of India
42.x: The 2024 amendment defined biodegradable plastics and required CPCB certification for their makers.
xa: Compostable plastics must meet **IS/ISO 17088**.
**FSSAI** found microplastics in all tested sugar and salt samples — a different context.
Timeline: 2016 Rules → 2021 Amendment → 2022 EPR Guidelines → **2024** Amendment → 2026 Amendment.

42.s: Which one of the following is NOT included among the identified single-use plastic items listed for prohibition?
o: Plastic sticks used in ear buds
42.x: Plastic ear-bud sticks, plastic flags and thermocol for decoration are included in the listed SUP items. HDPE milk bottles are not included in that list.
42.tq: Find the item outside the specified SUP list rather than choosing a prohibited item.
xs: **HDPE milk bottles** are not in the SUP ban list — option **(3)** is the answer.
Banned items include **ear buds with plastic sticks**, **thermocol for decoration** and **plastic flags**.
xa: Also banned: balloon sticks, candy and ice-cream sticks, plates, cups, cutlery, straws, stirrers, **PVC banners under 100 microns**.
**HDPE** milk/shampoo bottles are **rigid** packaging under **EPR Category I**.
In force from **1 July 2022**.

42.s: Which authorities are primarily responsible for enforcing the identified single-use plastic ban?
o: Only the Ministry of Jal Shakti
SPCBs/PCCs and local bodies, supported by national and state task forces
Only the National Disaster Management Authority
Only municipal corporations in metropolitan cities
42.x: Enforcement involves State Pollution Control Boards or Pollution Control Committees and local bodies, along with a National Level Taskforce and State Special Task Forces.
42.tq: Identify the correct combination of implementing authorities.
xs: Enforcement lies with **SPCBs/PCCs and local bodies**, backed by a **National Level Taskforce** and **State Special Task Forces** — option **(2)** is correct.
No single ministry or only metro corporations enforce it.
xa: AP enforces its SUP and **120-micron** carry-bag ban with **Revenue, Police, PCB**.
AP seizures: **5,505.06 kg** carry bags + **3,571.40 kg** SUP (SES 2025-26).
**Guntur**: complete ban from **15 Aug 2026**; fines up to **₹5,000** via **'Swachh App'**.

42.s: The identified single-use plastic ban covers approximately what proportion of total plastic waste?
42.x: The ban covers only about 11% of total plastic waste.
42.tq: Recall the precise proportion rather than assuming that the ban covers all plastic waste.
xs: The SUP ban covers only **11%** of total plastic waste — option **(2)** is correct (CSE 2023).
**5%**, **25%** and **50%** are not the stated share — the ban's reach is limited.
xa: SUP ban in force **1 July 2022**; **19 items** per most notes.
**70%+** of recycled plastic is handled by informal workers; **NAMASTE** aims to formalise them.
Packaging outside the ban is covered by **EPR Guidelines 2022**.

42.s: Under the plastic-packaging EPR framework, what is the full form of 'PIBOs'?
42.x: EPR applies to Producers, Importers and Brand Owners (PIBOs) for plastic packaging not covered by the SUP ban.
xa: Framework: **EPR Guidelines 2022**, effective **July 2022**.
Recyclers generate **EPR certificates** on the **CPCB portal** and sell them to producers.
Fewer than **50%** of producers comply with EPR.

42.s: Under the plastic-packaging EPR framework, how does the recycled-content target for rigid plastics rise from 2025-26?
42.x: Rigid plastics go from 30% to 60%; flexible single-layer from 10% to 20%; multi-layered from 5% to 10%.

42.s: What do China's National Sword Policy of 2018 and Thailand's 2025 measure mainly restrict?
o: Domestic manufacture of all plastic products
42.x: China's National Sword Policy and Thailand's 2025 measure restrict imports of plastic waste.
42.tq: Identify the regulated activity rather than the broad environmental theme.
xs: China's **National Sword Policy (2018)** and **Thailand's 2025 ban** restrict **plastic waste imports** — option **(1)** is correct.
They do not target hospital use, domestic manufacture or microplastics in food.
xa: **Basel** amendment on **plastic waste** is now operative.
**Global Plastics Treaty** process began at **UNEA-5.2 (Nairobi, March 2022)**.
Transboundary issue = physical transfer of hazardous waste, often to **developing countries**.

42.s: UNEA-5.2, held in Nairobi in March 2022, adopted which resolution that led to the establishment of the Intergovernmental Negotiating Committee (INC)?
42.x: The UNEA-5.2 resolution titled “End Plastic Pollution” established the Intergovernmental Negotiating Committee.
42.tq: Use the exact title of the resolution rather than a broad subject description.
xs: **UNEA-5.2** (Nairobi, March 2022) adopted the resolution "**End Plastic Pollution**" — option **(3)** is correct.
It set up the **Intergovernmental Negotiating Committee (INC)**.
xa: INC venues: **Punta del Este, Paris, Nairobi, Ottawa, Busan (INC-5, 2024), Geneva (INC-5.2, Aug 2025)**.
No agreement — sticking points: **production caps**, chemicals of concern, finance.

42.s: Bisphenol A (BPA) is particularly associated with which resin-code category?
42.x: Resin code 7 ('others') includes polycarbonate, which releases bisphenol A (BPA), an endocrine disruptor. PET (1), PVC (3) and PP (5) are not the BPA-linked category.
42.tq: Link a chemical concern with the correct resin category.
xs: **BPA** is linked to resin code **7**, which includes **polycarbonate** — option **(2)** is correct.
**Polycarbonate** (hard bottles, containers) releases **bisphenol A**, an **endocrine disruptor**.
**PET (1)**, **PVC (3)** and **PP (5)** are not the BPA category.
xa: **PET** leaches additives when heated.
Resin codes: 1 PET, 2 HDPE, 3 PVC, 4 LDPE, 5 PP, 6 PS, 7 others.

42.s: Which standard must compostable plastics meet?
42.x: Compostable plastics must meet the IS/ISO 17088 standard.
42.tq: Recall the exact technical standard rather than a general environmental certification.
xs: Compostable plastics must meet **IS/ISO 17088** — option **(3)** is correct.
The notes name no other standard for compostable plastics.
xa: **PWM Amendment Rules 2024** defined **biodegradable plastics** and required **CPCB certification** for makers.
**PWM Amendment Rules 2026**: **QR-code traceability**; classes rigid, flexible, multi-layered.

42.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the INC-5.2 plastics treaty meeting?
o: It was held in Geneva in August 2025
It ended with adoption of a final treaty text
Production caps and finance were major sticking points
42.x: INC-5.2 ended without agreement because of disputes over production caps, chemicals of concern and finance; no treaty text was adopted.

42.s: What is the main target of SBM-Urban 2.0, implemented during 2021-26?
42.x: SBM-Urban 2.0, covering 2021-26, targets garbage-free cities.
42.tq: Separate the mission’s current target from the objectives of related urban programmes.
xs: SBM-U 2.0's goal is **"Garbage Free" cities** by **2026** — option **(2)** is correct.
SBM-U 2.0 runs **2021-26** and covers **all statutory towns**, not only riverfront or heritage cities.
xa: Launched **1 Oct 2021**; **₹1.41 lakh crore** over 5 years; **Centrally Sponsored**, all statutory towns.
Components: **100% source segregation**, door-to-door collection, **legacy dumpsite remediation**, C&D waste management.
**Garbage Free City** star ratings: **1, 3, 5 and 7** stars.

42.s: What are nurdles?
o: Secondary microplastics formed only by tyre wear
Primary microplastic pellets generally measuring 1–5 mm
Biodegradable plastic fibres used in clothing
42.x: Nurdles are primary microplastic pellets, generally 1–5 mm in size.
42.tq: Distinguish a specific microplastic form from its sources and effects.
xs: **Nurdles** are **primary microplastic pellets** of **1-5 mm** — option **(2)** is correct.
**Tyre-wear** microplastics come from **synthetic rubber** — a different source.
xa: India's **first major nurdle landing**: **Kerala**, from the **MSC Elsa 3** shipwreck (LDPE, HDPE).
Microplastics = particles **up to 5 mm** (APPSC-GS 2023).

42.s: Up to what size are plastic particles generally called microplastics?
42.x: Microplastics are particles up to 5 mm (APPSC-GS 2023). 'Up to 5 micrometres only' is far too narrow, while 5-50 cm and above 5 mm describe larger debris.
42.tq: Micro = up to 5 mm; nurdles 1-5 mm.
xs: Microplastics are particles **up to 5 mm** — option **(1)** is correct (APPSC-GS 2023).
"**Above 5 mm**" and **5-50 cm** describe larger debris; "5 micrometres only" is far too narrow.
xa: **Nurdles** = primary microplastic pellets, **1-5 mm**.
Hidden sources: **tea bags, chewing gum, wet wipes, glitter, cigarette filters, polyester clothing**.

42.s: Which was the first country to ban thin plastic bags, in 2002?
42.x: Bangladesh banned thin plastic bags in 2002; New Zealand's supermarket produce-bag ban came in July 2023.
xa: ⚠ **Bangladesh** = first country (thin bags); **New Zealand** = first, thin produce bags in supermarkets.
India's **first major nurdle landing** was in **Kerala**, from the **MSC Elsa 3** shipwreck.
**Maharashtra** is the highest solid-waste-generating State (APPSC-G2 **2025** key).

42.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: LDPE/HDPE — carry bags and milk bottles
42.x: Synthetic rubber is associated with tyres, not drinking-water bottles. LDPE/HDPE, synthetic polymers and cellulose acetate have the associations shown in the other options.
42.tq: Find the product-material mismatch among familiar plastic applications.
xs: **Synthetic rubber — drinking-water bottles** is wrongly matched — option **(1)** is the answer.
Synthetic rubber is used in **tyres** and gives **tyre-wear microplastics**; water bottles are **PET**.
The others are correct: **cellulose acetate** — cigarette filters; **synthetic polymers** — chewing-gum base; **LDPE/HDPE** — carry bags, milk bottles.
xa: **Polycarbonate** — hard bottles; releases **BPA**.
**Microplastics**: particles **up to 5 mm** (APPSC-GS 2023).

42.s: Under the PWM Amendment Rules, 2021, what was the minimum carry-bag thickness from 30 September 2021?
42.x: 75 microns applied from 30 September 2021 and 120 microns from 31 December 2022.
42.tq: one-liner

42.s: What carry-bag thickness did the Plastic Waste Management Rules, 2016 set?
42.x: The 2016 Rules set 50 microns; the 2011 Rules had 40 microns.

42.x: The PWM Rules 2016 brought the 50-micron limit, a PWM fee and promoted plastic roads.

42.x: 19 identified single-use plastic items were banned from 1 July 2022; the ban covers only about 11% of plastic waste.

42.x: On the CPCB EPR portal, recyclers generate tradable EPR certificates.

42.x: New Zealand banned thin produce bags in July 2023; Bangladesh was first to ban thin bags (2002).

42.x: Code 1 PET, 2 HDPE, 3 PVC, 4 LDPE, 5 PP, 6 PS, 7 others incl. polycarbonate.
